### 248.5 What this revives, and the corrected closure threshold

```
a STREAM-class item is dead below   0.160 % LOCAL
a LATENCY-class item is dead below  0.067 % LOCAL   (0.115 % on the published floor)
```

Every item I closed between those two bounds was closed on the wrong test.

- **fused residual + RMSNorm. REVIVED.** Dose-measured 298.01 us/pass/round,
  R2 0.9506. Local 0.234 %, which is below the 0.277 % published floor and is
  why E96 rung 3a closed it. Ranked **0.561 %**, which is 2.0x the published
  floor and 3.5x the serial-free floor.
- **SDPA over the full-attention history.** I carried it at "0.4 % to 0.6 %
  corrected". Isolated ranked 2.386 %; discounted **0.92 % to 1.45 %**. It is
  the largest single latency item. 16 dispatches per round at 79.19 us each is
  far above launch overhead, so this is inefficiency, not launch cost: 4 kv
  heads x 2 x 1024 x 256 x 2 B = 4.2 MB per layer per round, 67 MB per round,
  at 79.19 us implies about 53 GB/s, which is 19 % of peak. Because it is
  inefficiency rather than pure launch, its true transfer factor sits between
  0.46 and 0.98; at a conservative 0.7 it is still 0.64 % to 1.01 % ranked.
- **GDN prework.** Local 0.426 %, ranked 1.023 % isolated, **0.40 % to 0.62 %**
  discounted.
- q/k norm + RoPE 0.11 % to 0.17 % discounted. Marginal.

- **GDN recurrent step stays closed.** It is stream-class at 212.5 GB/s, 77.8 %
  of peak, so its percentage does not amplify: dose 861 us = 0.675 % local and
  0.745 % ranked. There is little headroom at 78 % of peak, and rung 0 proved
  the scored path reaches the non-editable `GatedDelta.swift` copy.

### 248.6 THEME 6 — the small-dispatch and low-efficiency pool

New campaign theme, worth **2.0 % to 3.3 % published**, third largest after
Theme 1 (bytes per weight, 4.7 % to 5.5 %) and Theme 2a (streams per round).

The mechanism behind the whole pool is dispatch count and occupancy at M=5.
The activation tensors are tiny: [5, 5120] bf16 is 51 KB, which cannot fill a
20-core GPU, so these kernels run at 10 % to 19 % of peak. There are about 240
such dispatches per round. At the FACT 8 measured GPU dispatch boundary of
3.87 us [2.63, 5.11] that is about 929 us per round of pure boundary cost,
which is 1.75 % of the ranked round on its own.

Sub-items, ranked, with their collision risk:

1. **SDPA over FA history**, 0.64 % to 1.45 %. GQA pair-head K/V reuse in
   `sdpa_vector` at D=256, or an M=5-aware path. Lives in the steel attention
   sources. **Independent of all live work.**
2. **residual + RMSNorm prologue fusion into the quantized GEMM**, 0.56 %.
   Each GEMM threadgroup already reads the whole K=5120 activation row, so it
   can compute the RMS reduction itself from data it is already loading; the
   cost is one extra pass over an L2-resident 51 KB buffer.
   **COLLIDES with E100: alphonse is editing
   `qwen_fast_crossrow_affine4_g64_wide` in the same file. Do not assign until
   E100 resolves.**
3. **GDN prework**, 0.40 % to 0.62 %. Fuse into the recurrent step. Independent.
4. q/k norm + RoPE, 0.11 % to 0.17 %. Fold into the KV write. Independent.

### 248.7 What this does NOT change

E98, E99 and E100 are all stream-class or schedule-class mechanisms whose
percentages transfer at 1.0, and E99 is already priced directly on the ranked
curve. No live assignment's stop rule moves. The one thing every student must
change is the threshold they compare a small kernel's LOCAL cost against:
0.067 % local for latency-class work, not 0.160 %.

The head-side affine-2 metadata idea is a genuine byte change, so 0.236 remains
correct there and its 0.17 % shelving stands. Thorfinn flagged that himself.

false>`, emitted by `research/jit_string_compile.py --emit` and patched by

```
(c) constant  32 B   scale and bias as literals, timing-only upper bound
```

One process, one device, one command queue, three pipelines, order `ABCCBA`,
8 blocks per cell, 21 cells, 168 timing blocks, inner count auto-calibrated to
40 ms, first probe discarded, first cell run twice and dropped. Dispatch
matches `quantized.cpp` exactly: `grid_dims(M, (N+7)/8, 1)`,
`group_dims(32, 2, 1)`.

of up to 1,986,560 outputs per cell. Positive control, perturb

reference `a_vs_double_rms_over_signal` 2.8e-3 to 6.7e-3, the bf16 output
quantum. **The R4 encoding I designed is lossless in the kernel.** That is the
one positive result of the experiment.

```
gate_up   5  crossrow_m  2   760.59   763.35   745.96    -0.36%   +1.92%  -0.189
gate_up   8  crossrow_m  2   958.10   993.77   969.88    -3.72%   -1.23%   3.029
```

**The instrument is calibrated, so the null is real.** At M = 1 the probe
returns `(a)-(c)` 9.97 % to 11.42 % against the 11.1 % byte prediction and
`(a)-(b)` 5.18 % to 5.77 % against 5.56 %. The `ratio` column is 0.49 to 0.53
in every `G = 1` cell, exactly what a pure bandwidth model predicts because the
index removes half the metadata bytes. M = 2 `crossrow<T,2>` agrees. The probe
converts bytes to time at 1:1 wherever the kernel is byte limited, and returns
near zero at M >= 3 because the kernel is not byte limited there.

**LUT residency is not the cause.** A 64-entry, 256-byte, unconditionally
L1-resident table reproduces the 2,658-entry result within 0.25 pp
(lm_head M = 5 -0.33 %, gate_up M = 5 -0.31 %). A free lookup would still lose,
because arm (c) has no lookup and no metadata bytes and still reaches only
+1.9 % at M = 5.

**Registers.** `peak_live_regs` a = 163, b = 163, delta 0, c = 155.
`peak_live_values` 90 / 90 / 82, `device_loads` 858 / 931 / 712. The indexed
read costs zero registers, so the loss is not register pressure. Entry-point
scope with all width branches inlined, so the E46/E59 per-cell ceiling of 108
does not apply and only the arm delta is meaningful.

**Ceiling.** E96 streaming share 0.886 times the measured M = 5 mean
`(a)-(c)` of 1.91 % gives 1.69 % of round for removing all metadata and 0.85 %
for the pair index with a free lookup, against a 1.5 % minimum useful effect.
Measured is -0.35 %.

Caveats recorded by the student and accepted: arm (c) removes instructions as
well as bytes, so 1.9 % is an upper bound on pure byte removal, which
strengthens the kill; arm (c) is negative at M = 8, so those cells are schedule
limited and no byte model applies in either direction; NAX is untestable on
gen 16, and decode `qmv` never uses NAX; the isolated blocking eval is 2 % to
10 % pessimistic in absolute terms and that bias cancels in the contrast.

Gates verbatim: `harness=local`, `timing_valid=false`,
`cool_gate_passed_real_gate=false`, `gate_qualified_for_timing=false`. Temps
36.1 -> 55.9 C. Host Apple M4 Pro 20-core 48 GiB `applegpu_g16s` gen 16, Swift
6.3.3, Metal 32023.883, base `4d937ce3`. Budget unchanged, source
2,515,544 / 3,000,000, growth 60,709 / 262,144.
`verify-ranked-score-boundary.sh` PASS.

### 249.2 FINDING 23 - byte-share pricing over-prices by about 5x in this kernel family

Adopted campaign-wide, in the student's own words:

> In the `qmv_fast_crossrow_affine4_g64_m` and `_wide` family, logical byte
> share multiplied by achieved bandwidth over-prices byte-reduction work by
> about 5x. The correct discriminator is not "is the kernel near peak
> bandwidth". It is "does the removed byte reach DRAM once per read, or is it
> replayed from cache".

The cells read at 88.7 % to 98.9 % of the 273 GB/s peak **on logical bytes**
(lm_head M = 5 at 269.9 GB/s) and still return only about 0.17 of the predicted
time for an 11.1 % logical byte cut. The cross-row kernel amortises each
metadata word over IPG rows and holds it in cache, so metadata is logical
traffic, not DRAM traffic.

Alphonse reached the same conclusion independently from the board on the same
morning, from the other direction: the board's realisation factor for a
bytes-model prediction is `rho = 0.204`, and the largest local prediction in
his set (M = 6, -6.977 %) has the smallest measured ranked effect (-0.334 %).

**Consequences.**

1. **Theme 1, bytes per weight, is CLOSED.** Not because the encoding is wrong,
   which it is not, but because the scored kernel does not convert those bytes
   into time.
2. Finding 21's 88.6 % streaming share and 249.55 GB/s remain correct as a
   *census of where round time goes*. They are **not** a licence to price a
   byte removal at `byte_share x streaming_share`. Those are different
   questions and I conflated them.
3. Every remaining byte-reduction idea is repriced or shelved: the 12-bit
   packed index, the head-side affine-2 metadata index, entropy coding, and
   any future "remove bytes from the weight stream" proposal. **Before any of
   them is assigned again, the proposer must first run an M = 1 calibration
   cell and an arm (c) upper bound at the scored width.**
4. Finding 22's stream-class transfer factor of 1.00 still holds for work whose
   removed bytes genuinely reach DRAM. Finding 23 says: prove that first.

#### The hypothesis and the escape

**On `applegpu_g17s`, instantiating `NA = 5` in the shared `affine_qmv_fast`
entry point crosses an occupancy step that `applegpu_g16s` does not cross.**

Supporting: E88's FACT 17, g17s registers rise at all eight live cells where
g16s machine text shrinks 29 % to 40 %; E97's g16s AIR census at
`rows_per_simd = 4` gives na4 = 104 and **na5 = 125 against a 128 wall**, three
registers of margin; E76's `metal-tt` g17s counts give NA = 4 -> 91,
NA = 5 -> 98, NA = 6 -> 111; askeladd's E98 entry-point-scope count with every
branch inlined gives 163. **Three instruments, three numbers, unreconciled.**

The escape. The dominant register consumer is `acc[rows_per_simd][NA]`:

```
today       rows_per_simd = 4, NA = 4  ->  16 accumulators
proposed    rows_per_simd = 2, NA = 5  ->  10
proposed    rows_per_simd = 2, NA = 6  ->  12
proposed    rows_per_simd = 2, NA = 8  ->  16
```

At `rows_per_simd = 2`, `NA = 8` costs the same accumulator budget as today's
`NA = 4`. If the rest of the frame scales the same way, an arm exists that
instantiates every width up to `NA = 8` without raising the shared register
maximum at all, which by construction removes the suspected tax.

stop-list negative; 4 -> 2 is untried and is now the primary arm.

### 249.10 FINDING 26 - vibecodooor's mechanism, and an independent ranked calibration of Finding 22

`51b9bf85` starts from our promoted commit `23ef7556` and changes only the
proposal head's final exact-evaluation tail. From the upstream diff it:

- deletes `qwen35DraftRerankKernel`, the 32-lane value/id reducer;
- deletes the `gatherQuantizedMM` over 32 independent `N=1` affine-4 rows,
  together with the `_compactDraftGatherW/S/Z/Lhs` batch views and the
  `MLX_E85_GATHER_QMM` gate;
- adds one 256-thread kernel
  `qwen_mtp_draft_selected_affine4_rerank_g64_v1`. Eight SIMDgroups own four
  selected rows each, read those rows straight out of the full `[98336, 640]`
  packed matrix, run the established affine-4/group-64 `qmv_fast_impl`
  arithmetic, `simd_sum`, round through BF16, and then one SIMDgroup applies
  the incumbent strict total order and the unchanged `PREFIX_COUNT` /
  `CONTROL_OFFSET` mapping;
- moves the `qwen35Top32RealCount` / `qwen35Top32K` drift guard from inside the
  dense fallback branch to the top of `draftTokenIDWithDeclaredRerank`.

Decomposition, same instrument:

```
schedule identical on all eight prompts    YES
candidate leg   vibe faster by   +0.0268 %   sd 0.0730   (unweighted over 8)
serial leg      vibe slower by   +0.1956 %   sd 0.3346
serial-free     ours 3.33711595   vibe 3.33979539   gap  +0.0803 %
```

Per prompt the mechanism is `beagle +0.0477 %`, `essays +0.1103 %`,
`medicine +0.0747 %`, `republic +0.0634 %`, `botany +0.0190 %`,
`travel +0.0355 %`, `drama −0.0042 %`, `plutarch −0.1318 %`. Under Finding 16
the published statistic is `0.5 x beagle + 0.5 x min(essays, medicine,
republic, botany)`, and the fifth-ranked prompt here is essays, so the median
pair moves `(0.0477 + 0.1103) / 2 = +0.079 %`, which reproduces the measured
`+0.0803 %`. **Eight-ninths of their headline is the serial lottery.**

🔴 **This is the calibration Finding 22 was missing.** Their removal is on the
order of one net dispatch plus a launch-geometry change; Finding 4 puts
`affine_gather_qmv` plus the top-32 finalize at 29.64 µs per draft combined,
so the removal is roughly 10 to 15 µs per draft. The Finding 22 latency table

at 10 to 15 µs. **Measured `+0.0803 %`.** An independent rival receipt lands at
the low end of our predicted band. Finding 22's latency-class pricing survives
a test it could have failed, and it does not repeat advisor error 53.

The consequence for E101 is direct. Thorfinn's chain C is a 42.6 to 104.21

**FINDING 27, in four parts.**

**27a. The dispatcher allocates exactly what its widest inlined body
allocates**, in 7 of 7 arms on both generations, including the 16-byte g16s
spill frame at NA=6. The `switch (ntg.x)` adds no pressure. Alphonse's Fact 1
raised the right question and the answer is that E76's and E97's body-scope
censuses were the correct instrument all along.

**27b. `peak_live_regs` is not a register count and must stop being read as
one.** It counts SSA values live at a point in architecture-independent AIR,
before any AGX backend runs. It sits 1.7x above the machine allocation at body
scope and 1.8x at entry-point scope. It preserves arm order - A 163 < C 182 <
B 183 < D 201 matches g17s 91 < 98 = 98 < 111 - so it is a valid **relative
screen and never a level**. The campaign has been quoting 163 and 125 as though
they were registers.

> 🔴 **SITE INDEX, ledger 258.** Every earlier `peak_live_regs` figure in this
> file is an SSA-liveness screen, never a machine register count, and must be
> read through 27b. The affected sites are lines **3269, 5035, 5250, 8332,
> 10896, 11259, 18595, 29691 and 30354**. Line 18837 already withdraws E38's
> `peak_live_regs = 144`. The `20 + 21*max(NA) + 4*[two distinct NA group
> sizes]` law at lines 10896 and 11259 remains a valid ORDERING law in AIR and
> is not a register budget: the real budgets are **96 on g16s and 124 on g17s**
> (FINDING 34), read from the compiled pipeline, and only those two numbers may
> be used to reason about occupancy through `S_ranked(R) = floor(496 KiB /
> (128 R))`. E110 session A adds the harder lesson: even a true machine register
> count is a screen and never a ranking, because an arm that changes the unroll
> decision can cut registers and machine text while running 2.8x slower
> (ADVISOR ERROR 66, RULE 36b).

**27c. The runtime `MTLComputePipelineState` arbiter is saturated.** Every arm
and every body cell reports `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup = 1024`,
`threadExecutionWidth = 32`, `staticThreadgroupMemoryLength = 0`, and the device
maximum is also 1024. 91, 98 and 111 registers all still permit a full
1024-thread threadgroup, so the field cannot move. `metal-tt` is the only
instrument that separates the two generations. Reported as a null instrument
rather than dressed as a confirmation.

**27d. Dead-width pruning is dead.** A, E and F are byte-identical GPU objects,
g16s digest `8c9c4255`, g17s digest `44096e70`. The compiler already folds the
emptied `case 9:` into `default:`, so there is no separable switch-shape
effect. G also keeps 94/91. Pruning moves only machine text, `126,984 ->
121,174 -> 114,736` g17s bytes, which converts to `0.0000 %` under the
E77-corrected law. Rung 2 closed with a negative and not built.

**Also settled: B and C are identical in registers and pipeline properties.**
The unreachable `<T,9,5,true>` costs zero registers and 9.6 KB of cold text.
Dropping it is right and its prize is zero. It is not why `ca9251b8` lost.

🔴 **The headline is the first zero-parameter ranked prediction this campaign
has made.** Applying the E77-corrected law, `S(R) = floor(496 KiB / 128 R)`
and `Omega = (32 / S)^0.01346`, arm B sits at `R = 98`, `S = 40`, a
`+0.0974 %` cost against arm A on **every** QMV dispatch at **every** width.

Against a within-mode per-run serial-free sd of 0.113 %, the G = 1 half is
fully explained with no fitted parameter. **A widening confined to one width
still taxes every other width, because the entry point is shared.** Every
future kernel proposal in this campaign must price that flat tax before it
prices its own gain.

The G = 2 residual is unexplained and points the wrong way. Only M = 5 and the

M = 9 is unreachable under `segmentedVerifyDepthCap = 7`.

🔴 **Delete the ledger-248 headline that Theme 2a covers "M5 + M6 + M7 + M8 =
77 % of width mass".** The honest ceiling is the M = 5 round share times the
M = 5 gain, and the ledger-207 M = 5 share is 24.1 %.

legs `all_tokens_matched=true`, `residual_divergence_count=0`, identical
`effective_mean_draft_len 6.376623` and `accepted_draft_rate 0.885947`:

| leg | arm | candidate s/tok |
|---|---|---:|

| w512-a1 | base | 0.03373135 |
| w512-a2 | base | 0.03374217 |
| w512-b2 | collapse | 0.03373426 |

Arm means base `0.03373676`, collapse `0.03376875`, **collapse `+0.095 %`**
against a base within-arm spread of 0.032 % and a collapse spread of 0.204 %.
The 64-token sessions closed at depth 8 `+0.167 %` and depth 4 `−0.098 %`.

**ADVISOR ERROR 56.** I pre-registered `−6 %` to `−12 %` at depth 4 and
`−0.5 %` to `−1.5 %` at depth 8 on 512 tokens. Both are refuted on the wrong
side. I built the band by multiplying an isolated-cell effect by a streaming
share, which is exactly the error Finding 23 named and which I then committed
again. Alphonse's round reconstruction is the better instrument.

**His 17x discrepancy is the real finding.** His probe reconstructs the target
forward pass from measured per-shape cell costs and layer counts and tracks the
measured round well on the base arm: 54.15 ms at M = 1, 114.68 ms at M = 5,
123.94 ms at the depth-8 mean width of 6.4, against a measured 154.87 ms round
that also carries drafting, SDPA and state work. It does **not** track the
collapse arm: it predicts the M = 5 forward falls `114.68 -> 89.40 ms`, a
25.3 ms saving, and the depth-4 session measures **1.47 ms**.

Two readings: the scored decode does not reach the wide `affine_qmv_fast`
dispatch, or it reaches it with the second weight stream already resident.

**The decisive controls, promoted above the remaining timed leg.** Alphonse
designed a dose control - change `case 6` to `<T, 6, 2, true>`, legal today
with no `static_assert` change and no register change, splitting M = 6 into
three x-groups instead of two, which must slow the depth-8 round by roughly
30 % if the path is reached and each pass costs full DRAM. I promoted it to
first and split it, because the control alone separates "each pass costs full
DRAM" from the other two readings but does **not** separate "path not reached"
from "second pass cache-served", and those two have opposite consequences.

1. **Name census, free, no timing.** One `MLX_E58_BUFFER_LIMIT_OPS=0`
   `MLX_E58_BUFFER_LIMIT_MB=1` census leg at forced depth 4 and one at forced
   depth 5 on the unmodified tip, reporting the verbatim dispatched kernel name
   strings. The JIT name carries the template parameters.
2. **Dose leg**, as he designed it, with an immediate revert and the census
   name reported in both arms so the arm is witnessed in the leg.

All three outcomes are publishable and all three change what the other students
do next. If the answer is "path not reached", E76, E97, E98 and E102 all
measured an unexecuted path and the campaign re-prices. If it is
"cache-served", Finding 21's DRAM-floor picture is wrong at G = 2 and Theme 1
stays closed for a second and stronger reason. If it is `+30 %`, E100 closes as
a clean mechanism-level negative.

**Alphonse withdrew the noise claim** on the `ca9251b8` receipt after my
`research/board_na5_verdict.py` contrast, accepting that a delta growing

working G collapse. His corpus result stands as a statement about the
population of stream removals at NA <= 4; the within-mode sd of 0.113 % is the
right instrument for that specific pair.

### 250.1 FINDING 28 - the harness never rebuilds the worker binary, and the JIT quantized family is served from it

Alphonse, PR #102, comment `e100-retraction-and-first-valid-arm`.

For the `quantized` kernel family the metallib is dead. The chain is:

```
jit_kernels.cpp:915   get_quantized_kernel() -> d.get_library(lib_name, builder)
device.cpp:770        that overload calls build_library_(builder()) directly and
                      never opens default.metallib
metal::quantized()    the R"preamble(...)" literal in mlx-generated/quantized.cpp,
                      linked into .build-worker/release/mlxfast-runtime-worker
Package.swift:284     excludes nojit_kernels.cpp and compiles jit_kernels.cpp
```

So the kernel source that actually runs is the string compiled into the worker
binary. `benchmark-qwen-mtp.sh:200-206` extracts only
`metallib_rebuild_required()` from `benchmark.sh`; it never extracts
`swift_build_required()` at `benchmark.sh:1791-1806` and never reaches the
worker build at `benchmark.sh:1842`. A run therefore rebuilds `mlx.metallib`,
reports success, and times the previous binary.

Timestamp proof read at 13:17 GMT: twin `quantized.cpp` 13:03:36, `mlx.metallib`
13:04:36, object `quantized.cpp.o` **2026-08-20 21:11:03**, worker **2026-08-21
10:44:44**. A forced `swift build --scratch-path .build-worker` flipped the
template from `<T,5,3,true>` to `<T,5,5,true>` and produced worker
`2a5d30ab64ac6430d05071a58f687be033b7f88842c9c62f594f45ea20c120a7`.

**This is harness defect 12 and it retracts four reported E100 nulls**
(+0.167 %, −0.098 %, +0.095 %, −0.016 %). They are one unchanged build measured
eight times. The 17x to 840x probe-to-end-to-end discrepancy is withdrawn.

Standing rule adopted for the campaign: **no timed kernel leg may be reported
unless `senpai/rebuild-and-assert-worker.sh` has asserted the arm string inside
the binary immediately before the leg, and the analysis refuses any leg whose
binary template counts do not match its arm.** Alphonse implemented this in
`research/e100_e2e_leg.sh` at commit `64b37243`; `meta.txt` now carries
`worker_mtime_pre/post`, `worker_sha256_pre/post` and four template counts.

Trap for anyone reusing that guard: it matches with `grep -c --`, so the needle
is a regular expression. `NA in [2, 5]` is a character class and matches
nothing.

Triage of what else the defect could have touched, so no student spends legs on
it: **E76 sections 3 to 5 are not at risk** (arms separated by +14.16 % to
+64.71 %, and three independent ranked trees agree); **E97 and E98 are not at
risk** (in-process JIT pipelines built inside the measuring process); **E102 is
not at risk** (CPU only, no GPU timing). Only E100 was affected.

### 250.3 FINDING 29 - the within-run width tax, a 0.509 pp ranked instrument for zero GPU seconds

Committed as `research/board_width_tax.py`.

For one scored run form

```
W = mean over the five G=2 prompts of log(mtp_seconds_per_token)
  - mean over the three G=1 prompts of log(mtp_seconds_per_token)
```

and compare it only inside a cohort of runs whose eight per-prompt
`effective_mean_draft_len` values are bit-identical, so every run in the cohort
offers the same eight verify-width mixes.

Why it is sharp:

1. It uses only the candidate leg, so the serial-baseline lottery of Finding 20
   cannot enter it.
2. Any run-level common shift cancels exactly. The FACT 2 measurement mode,
   thermal state and a uniform per-kernel register tax all scale both terms.
3. The FACT 2 mode very nearly cancels as well. It costs about 0.601 ms per
   *drafting* round: about +1.0 % of a `G = 2` round, and +1.5 % on drama,
   +1.44 % on travel and +0.15 % on plutarch, mean +1.03 %, on the `G = 1` side.

**Measured resolution: `sd(W) = 0.509 pp` over a cohort of 215 runs at or above
3.15 sharing one schedule.** That implies a per-prompt residual of 0.697 %
after the run effect is removed, consistent with alphonse's rung 0 corpus,
where one whole candidate leg carries 1.077 %. The instrument is about four
times finer than the Finding 6 published floor on the same quantity.

A second observation from the same cohort machinery, worth its own follow-up:
in the 79-run **crown-schedule** cohort the per-prompt cohort standard
deviations are plutarch **0.088 %**, drama 0.964 %, travel 1.188 %, beagle
0.876 %, republic 0.869 %, essays 0.820 %, medicine 0.860 %, botany 1.027 %.
Plutarch draws only 38 drafting rounds out of 487, so its candidate leg is
almost pure `M = 1` decoding and is nearly immune to the FACT 2 mode.
**Within a homogeneous cohort the plutarch candidate leg resolves a change to
the non-drafting decode path at about 0.09 %.** That is the class of broad
target-runtime improvement that cancels in the local serial-to-MTP ratio and
that we have never been able to price. It should be built out next.

`_mN` family so the shared `_wide` stays at `NA <= 4`. `ca9251b8` at line 1939
is `qmv_fast_crossrow_affine4_g64_m<T, 5, 5, true>` with `case 6` untouched:

per-prompt log deviation from the cohort, minus the common shift measured on
plutarch, drama and travel.

| prompt | M | `3ff80e86` shape | `ca9251b8` shape |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| beagle | 5.533 | −0.297 pp | +0.169 pp |
| medicine | 5.768 | −0.310 pp | −0.174 pp |
| republic | 6.270 | −0.052 pp | +0.389 pp |
| essays | 6.425 | −0.315 pp | +0.481 pp |
| botany | 6.776 | −0.540 pp | −0.052 pp |
| **mean** | | **−0.303 pp** | **+0.163 pp** |
| `W` z | | −0.59 | +0.32 |

Four readings.

**(a) The f2 claim that both clean ranked controls point the wrong way is
withdrawn.** They point in opposite directions and `3ff80e86` is favourable.

**(b) Neither is individually significant.** Both sit inside ±0.6 sd and their
mean is **−0.070 ± 0.360 pp**, consistent with zero.

**(c) Zero is not what the mechanism predicts.** The ranked `M = 5` round is
53,108 us and the second stream at that width is worth 5,951 us, 11.21 % of the
round. At alphonse's realisation factor of 0.72 that is 8.07 % per `M = 5`
round. These two trees run at `M̄ = 5.53` to `6.78`, so an `M = 5` share of 15
to 20 % predicts a shape of −1.2 to −1.6 pp. Measured −0.070 pp. **The
prediction sits about 3.7 sd from the measurement.**

**(d) Neither tree shows the width ordering the mechanism requires.** An
`M = 5`-only collapse must help beagle at `M̄ = 5.53` most and botany at
`M̄ = 6.78` least. `3ff80e86` runs the other way; `ca9251b8` has no order.

**Where the disagreement most likely lives.**

| machine | `M = 4` round | `M = 5` round | second stream | share of one 14.4 GB pass |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| local M4 Pro | 86,237 us | 126,103 us | 39,866 us | **0.755** |
| ranked M5 | 43,162 us | 53,108 us | 9,946 us | **~0.33** |

Locally the second pass is barely overlapped and costs three quarters of a
first pass; on the ranked runner it costs about a third. Removing a pass can
only pay what that pass costs. This is E54's lone-group table again: a single
`NA = 5` group achieves 150.9 GB/s while two concurrent groups reach 228.6 GB/s
through `MTL::DispatchTypeConcurrent`. **A bandwidth-rich machine loses more
memory-level parallelism when the groups are collapsed than a bandwidth-poor
one does.**

A defect in my own ranked curve must be recorded beside this. The `G = 1` line
`27,181.5 + 3,995.1 M` is fitted across plutarch, drama and travel, whose
drafting fractions differ by more than an order of magnitude - plutarch draws
38 drafting rounds out of 487. Extrapolating it to `M = 5` to price the
collapse is not sound, and the gap between its 3,995 us per-row slope and the
`G = 2` line's 7,233 us is the symptom. **The 5,951 us second-stream figure is
an upper bound with an unquantified error, not a measurement.**

**Edward then showed that these figures carry no run-to-run variance at all.**
He hashed the full `(round, depth, accepted)` sequence of eight arm-and-cap
replicate pairs; all eight are bit-identical. Decoding is greedy and the
schedule reads only model state, so on a fixed prompt the round sequence is a
deterministic function of the arm, and the ranked-curve figure
`sum_r C(d_r + 1) / sum_r (a_r + 1)` is a pure function of that sequence. His
two cap-8 arm-off legs did not agree to within noise; they returned the
identical value 10655.4. **`+3.22 %` against `+3.01 %` is an exact difference
of the schedule, not two draws.** Replication can only sharpen the wall clock.

He also refuted my rung 7 falsification arm. I proposed clamp depth 4 as the
arm that would kill the stream-boundary account. It cannot: the two ranked
lines cross at `M = 3.162`, so the pure discontinuity at `M = 4` is only
2,713 us and the rest of the 9,946 us gap is one ordinary unit of `G = 2`
slope. At `M >= 5` the real curve and a no-step control are the same line, so
depth 4 and depth 5 give identical predictions under both accounts to four
decimal places. His replacement discriminator is **`gain(depth 2) −
gain(depth 3)`**: the stream-boundary account predicts about −0.73 pp with the
ordering `d3 > d2 > d4 > d1`, and the drafting-cost-only account predicts about
+0.44 pp with the ordering `d2 > d1 > d3 > d4`. Depth 1 is the single most
discriminating arm at 1.63 pp. Pre-registered replay on the ranked M5 curve at

### 251.1 FINDING 31 - the round is an identity in `G / rate(partition)`

Every measured local round time is reproduced to better than 0.03 % by

```
round_us  =  G  x  14.41235 GB  /  rate(partition)
```

where `G` is the number of x-groups, 14.41235 GB is the transformed weight set,
and `rate` is the aggregate achieved bandwidth of that partition.

| M | partition | G | predicted us | measured us | residual |
|--:|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | `[1]` | 1 | 64,455 | 64,445 | 0.016 % |
| 2 | `[2]` | 1 | 69,760 | 69,776 | 0.023 % |
| 3 | `[3]` | 1 | 74,791 | 74,778 | 0.017 % |
| 4 | `[4]` | 1 | 86,250 | 86,237 | 0.015 % |
| 5 | `[3+2]` | 2 | 126,090 | 126,103 | 0.010 % |

This is not a fit. It is a restatement of Finding 21 (the round is 88.6 % DRAM
weight streaming) with the residual folded into `rate`. Its value is that it
separates the two things a partition change can do: change `G`, or change
`rate`. Every prior discussion of the G boundary confused the two.

The rate table is the campaign's most important new object.

| partition | M | local GB/s | vs NA=1 | ranked GB/s | vs NA=1 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `[1]` | 1 | 223.6 | 1.000 | 462.3 | 1.000 |
| `[2]` | 2 | 206.6 | 0.924 | 409.8 | 0.886 |
| `[3]` | 3 | 192.7 | 0.862 | 368.0 | 0.796 |
| `[4]` | 4 | 167.1 | 0.747 | 333.9 | 0.722 |
| `[3+2]` | 5 | 228.6 | 1.022 | 542.8 | 1.174 |
| `[3+3]` | 6 | 209.1 | 0.935 | 477.7 | 1.033 |
| `[4+3]` | 7 | 191.6 | 0.857 | 426.6 | 0.923 |
| `[4+4]` | 8 | 175.8 | 0.786 | 385.3 | 0.833 |
| `[3+3+3]` | 9 | 211.9 | 0.948 | - | - |

Two facts fall straight out.

**(a) Degradation with NA is real on both machines and slightly steeper on the
ranked one** (0.722 against 0.747 at NA=4). A repair should transfer.

**(b) The ranked box extracts far more from concurrent groups than the local box
does.** This is the whole story of the next section.

Overhead factors, taken as actual divided by `max(DRAM floor, FMA floor)`, where
the one-group DRAM floor is 14.41235 GB at 273 GB/s = 52,792 us and the NA=5 FMA
floor is 44,428 us (E97's 6.568 TFLOP/s less the 12.2 % dequant haircut):

| NA | local one-group round us | overhead |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 64,445 | 1.221x |
| 2 | 69,776 | 1.322x |
| 3 | 74,778 | 1.416x |
| 4 | 86,237 | 1.634x |
| 5 | 103,404 (measured, post-collapse) | 1.959x |

At NA=5 the kernel reads at roughly 55 % of DRAM peak and computes at roughly
47 % of the FMA ceiling **at the same time**. Neither resource is exhausted.
That is a latency or issue-rate problem, not a resource wall, and it is
therefore repairable in principle.

If NA=5 could be brought to the overhead NA=1 already demonstrates (1.221x), the
local one-group M=5 round would fall from 103,404 to 64,459 us, a 37.7 %
reduction on 24.1 % of rounds.

### 251.2 FINDING 32 - the group-scaling factor, and why the fewer-streams theme is dead on the official runner

Collapsing M=5 from `[3+2]` to `[5]` halves the bytes and removes one concurrent
instruction stream. Under Finding 31 the trade is exact:

```
time([3+2]) = 2W / r2        time([5]) = W / r1
collapse gain = 1 - r2 / (2 r1) = 1 - A/2 ,   A = r2 / r1
```

`A` is the group-scaling factor: the aggregate bandwidth of two x-groups divided
by that of one. **`A = 2` means the collapse is worth exactly nothing.** The
entire value of the fewer-streams theme is the distance of `A` below 2.

**Local, from alphonse's own measurement, no extrapolation.** `[3+2]` measures
126,103 us, so `r2 = 228.6 GB/s`. He measured the collapse at 17.5-18.6 % per
M=5 round; at 18.0 % the one-group round is 103,404 us, so `r1 = 139.4 GB/s`.

```
A_local = 228.6 / 139.4 = 1.640     collapse gain = +18.0 %
```

**Ranked, route 1 - uses no rival receipt.** Take the step from `[3]` to `[3+2]`
in our own ranked cost curve. Aggregate bandwidth scales x1.186 locally and
x1.475 on the ranked box, an advantage of x1.244. Applying that advantage:

```
A_ranked (predicted) = 1.640 x 1.244 = 2.040     collapse gain = -2.0 %
```

**Ranked, route 2 - the two rival receipts measure it directly.** `ca9251b8` is
alphonse's four lines almost verbatim; `3ff80e86` collapses M=5 only through a
private `_mN` family. The Finding 29 width tax `W` reads them at
`dW = -0.070 +/- 0.360 pp`. At an M=5 share of 0.24 of G=2 rounds:

```
M=5 round gain = -0.29 +/- 1.50 %
A_ranked (measured) = 1.994   [1.964, 2.024]
implied one-group rate at NA=5 = 272.2 GB/s = 50 % of the two-group 542.8
```

**Route 1 predicts 2.040. Route 2 measures 1.994. They agree, and they are
independent.**

Falsification margin, at the same 0.24 share:

| counterfactual | A | predicted gain | predicted dW | sigma from receipts |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ranked box keeps its own NA ladder | 1.862 | +6.9 % | -1.65 pp | **4.4** |
| ranked box behaves like the local box | 1.640 | +18.0 % | -4.32 pp | **11.8** |

The conclusion is robust to the share: even at 0.10 the conservative
counterfactual is still about 1.9 sigma, and every plausible combination of
share and realisation lands between 3 and 12 sigma.

### 252.3 FINDING 33 - a threshold sited in a gap is fragile, not robust

The margin distribution measured on the one public fixture is strongly bimodal:
`q0.10 = 1.25, q0.25 = 9.625, q0.50 = 14.25`. The shipped constant 9.4375 sits
at quantile 0.244, immediately below the dense region. Edward recorded in E99
interim 6 that it "sits in a gap in the data", and measured that t = 8.25 and
t = 9.4375 both return +3.22 % at cap 8.

**Both of us read that flatness as robustness. It is the exact opposite.**

A threshold sitting in a gap means a large mass of the distribution sits just
on one side of it. Insensitivity of the realised rate to the threshold is
therefore proof that a small shift of the distribution carries that whole mass
across at once. The hidden prompts have systematically lower top-2 margins
than the single public fixture, the mass crossed, and the fire rate went from

**The depth-price structure is set by a hardware dispatch boundary, not by
drafting cost.** This underwrites Finding 12, Finding 14 and Finding 31 and it
survives the gate's failure entirely.

He also refuted advisor error: I claimed depth 4 recovers close to zero, he
pre-registered 61.5 %, and it measured 57 %. And he was right that depth 4 and
depth 5 have literally zero discriminating power, because at M >= 5 the two
candidate curves are the same line by construction; that is why he added
depth 1, the most discriminating single arm at 1.63 pp.

**Methodological result, with its caveat.** Four replicates per arm gave one
distinct value on both arms, range 0.000 %, because the `(round, draft,
accept)` sequence is bit-identical. One leg per cell suffices for a
ranked-curve contrast. The caveat is the important half: **zero variance is not
accuracy.** The statistic is a deterministic function of a cost model, so it
repeats its own bias exactly. That is precisely how a confidently wrong local
number was produced.

**Correctness**: 16/16 legs matched exactly, zero DRAM-floor violations, zero
residual divergences, `dirty_candidate_paths=0`, ABBA counterbalanced, and

preserved verbatim.

`bj9zpvtw` `tan8623z` `ibgx90bh`. Report `research/e103-results.md`.

```
stacked ceiling   379 us/round = 0.2988 %   against a 0.300 % bar
ranked after 2.40x latency and the 1.65-2.59x in-situ discount:  0.277 - 0.435 %
whose low end IS the published detection floor to three decimals
```

He declined to start the integration. Correct call.

**The premise is falsified, and the reason generalises.** Redundant K/V traffic
is only 21.6 % of the dispatch and is served from cache at **835 to 1046 GB/s,
which is 3.1 to 3.8x DRAM peak**, so removing redundancy removes almost
nothing. The dispatch actually spends **26.3 % in softmax and 25.3 % in a
cross-simdgroup reduction tail**, neither of which head packing touches.

**Campaign consequence.** Every low-GB/s line in the Finding 22 reprice table
is now suspect in the same way. A census bandwidth figure computed on logical
bytes understates a cache-served dispatch by up to ~16x. **Before pricing any
latency-class fusion, measure the real achieved bandwidth in an isolated
harness.** This is now rung 0 of every latency-class assignment.

**Register wall on packing**: P=6 spills 400 bytes for +282 % cost; the usable
arm is P=2.

**Wave quantisation, promoted to a transfer hazard.** The 5+r merge is
bit-identical in all 16 cells with all 16 positive controls detected, and is
worth **7.54 us/dispatch, only 36 % of the 20.9 us a linear fit predicts**,
because `24*M` threadgroups against **20 cores** quantise into waves. The
ranked M5 has a different core count, so a dispatch that quantises badly
locally may not quantise badly on the ranked box, and the reverse. **Report
threadgroup count and implied waves against 20 cores for every measured
dispatch, and attribute any shortfall against a linear fit to quantisation
explicitly.**

**Post-E100 re-anchor, as instructed**: width-5 rounds shorten 18.6 % to
103,579 us, width-6 rounds are untouched at 139,476 us and carry 58.7 % of the
width mass, session-weighted round 126,771 us.

### 252.6 The E103 handoff, and FINDING 34 - the collapse break-even law

The handoff from the same census:

> `affine_qmv_fast` costs **116.60 us/row at M=5** but **136.11 us/row at M=6**,
> 6.7 to 18.3 % worse per row across all five shapes, worth **13,869 us/round at
> M=6** (9.94 % of that round) and about **8.1 ms/round session average, 21x
> E103's entire ceiling**.

The cause is structural and it is ours: E100 collapsed **M=5 only**, so a
width-5 round streams the weights once as `[5]` while a width-6 round still
streams them twice as `[3+3]`.

Finding 32 says a collapse is worth nothing ranked at `A_ranked = 2`. Combining
that with the collapse identity gives the useful operational form.

**FINDING 34.**

```
collapse gain = 1 - A/2 ,   A = r2 / r1
A_ranked = A_local x 1.244
ranked-neutral  <=>  A_ranked = 2  <=>  A_local = 2 / 1.244 = 1.6077
                <=>  r1_local = r2_local / 1.6077
```

Every verify width has a **break-even one-group local streaming rate**. Above
it the collapse pays on the ranked box; below it the collapse is a ranked loss
however good it looks locally. `research/collapse_breakeven.py`:

| M | partition today | `r2` local | **`r1` break-even** | `r1` measured | verdict |
|--:|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| 5 | `[5]` after E100 | 228.6 | **142.2** | **139.4** | 2.0 % short, -0.3 to -2.0 % ranked |
| 6 | `[3+3]` | 209.1 | **130.1** | not measured | unknown |
| 7 | `[4+3]` | 191.6 | **119.2** | not measured | unknown |
| 8 | `[4+4]` | 175.8 | **109.3** | not measured | unknown |

Two consequences.

**(a) Finding 32 is now a self-consistent model, not one measurement.** At M=5
the break-even is 142.2 and alphonse measured 139.4, a 2.0 % shortfall, which
predicts a small ranked loss. Finding 32's two independent ranked routes gave
-2.0 % and -0.3 +/- 1.5 %. The identity, the round measurement and the rival
receipts all agree. The model is now safe to price other experiments with.

**(b) The break-even threshold FALLS as M rises** - 142.2, 130.1, 119.2, 109.3
- because two wide concurrent groups themselves stream more slowly at higher
NA. The one-group rate also falls with NA. **Which falls faster is an open
empirical question and nobody has ever measured `r1` above NA = 5.**

Time-weighted over ranked round costs and the ledger-207 width shares:

```
M = 5      21.76 % of round time
M = 6      34.27 %
M >= 6     65.65 %
```

**The width we already collapsed is the small one.** This is now the highest-
value cheap measurement on the board and it has been folded into E104 rung 0.5.

### FINDING 35 - THE DISPATCH-TRANSFER CORRECTION (ADVISOR ERROR 61)

The measured ranked realisation for a launch-overhead-bound dispatch deletion is

```
ranked %  ~=  0.95 x local %          (percentage form)
ranked_delta_us ~= 0.52 x local_delta_us   (absolute form)
```

NOT the Finding 22 LATENCY value of `x2.40`. The overprediction factor is 2.52x.

Physics. The ranked M5 GPU dispatch boundary is about 1.3 us against the local
FACT-8 boundary of 3.87 us [2.63, 5.11], so `L_ranked ~= 0.42 x L_local`. The
ranked round is 2.40x shorter than the local round. The two effects nearly
cancel, which is why a dispatch deletion keeps its PERCENTAGE but loses more
than half of its absolute microseconds.

Two independent board measurements now support the 0.93-0.95 percentage
transfer for chain C (E101's selection chain):

1. frontier contrast `51b9bf85` vs `9612d3ba`: +0.1572 %, sd 0.0236, 8/8 positive.
2. isolated contrast `73cb7dfe` vs `9612d3ba`: +0.1515 %, sd 0.0983.

Local was -0.1651 %, so the transfer ratio is 0.93-0.95.

### FINDING 36 - THE PER-DISPATCH FIXED-COST LAW

Fit `dispatch_us = F + bytes_GB x S` to the four clean streaming families of the
E96 round census, converting each family to bytes through the shape table at
G=2 (weights streamed twice per round at M>=5), BPE = 0.5625.

```
family                     disp/rnd   GB/disp   us/disp     GB/s
lm_head                           2   0.71516   2634.66    271.4
mlp.gate_up                     128   0.10027    377.98    265.3
gdn.in_proj                      96   0.04746    184.12    257.8
fa.qkv                           32   0.04129    161.36    255.9

  S  =  3670.2 us per GB   ->  272.5 GB/s  =  99.8 % of the 273 GB/s DRAM peak
  F  =     9.90 us per dispatch

family                       us/disp  predicted  resid us  resid %
lm_head                      2634.66    2634.66     -0.01   -0.000
mlp.gate_up                   377.98     377.91      0.07    0.019
gdn.in_proj                   184.12     184.10      0.02    0.009
fa.qkv                        161.36     161.44     -0.08   -0.050

  R^2 = 1.00000000
```

Step 1 reconciliation: census GB/s against shape-table-implied GB/s agree to
-0.17 to -0.26 % on all five lines. The census is trustworthy.

CONSEQUENCE 1. There is NO bandwidth headroom anywhere in the target streaming
path at G=2. After removing F, all four clean families sit at 99.8-99.9 % of
DRAM peak. The census "rate deficits" of 97.2 %, 94.4 % and 93.7 % ARE the fixed
cost, not kernel inefficiency. "Make the QMV kernel stream faster" at G=2 is
CLOSED.

CONSEQUENCE 2. 514 streaming dispatches x 9.90 us = 5,091 us = 3.992 % of the
127,533 us local round is pure fixed cost. This total is invariant to whether
G=2 is two GPU dispatches (F = 9.90) or an internal loop in one dispatch
(F = 19.80): the product is the same.

CONSEQUENCE 3 - THE ANOMALY. `gdn.out_proj + fa.o_proj + mlp.down` is the only
family that misses the law.

```
family                        disp   GB/round   law us   measured us   excess us
gdn.out_proj + fa.o_proj       128     2.2649   9580.4
mlp.down                       128     6.4173  24820.2
combined                       256     8.6822  34400.6       36559.2      2158.6

  excess = 8.43 us/dispatch on top of the 9.90 us law
         = 5.90 % of the family
         = 1.693 % of the local round
  achieved peak after removing F:  93.5 %   (every other family: 99.8 %)
```

CONSEQUENCE 4 - PERFECT MONOTONE ORDERING IN N (output width):

| tensor              |     K |      N | census % peak | % peak after F |

**HIS FINDING 36 - AIR op counts do not predict time; ISA text size and spill
do.**

| arm | AIR FP ops/NA | g16s reg/spill @NA=5 | ISA text delta | NA=5 time delta | bit-exact cells |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| `xf_exactfma` | 112 | 92 / 0 | +0.2 % | -0.77 % | 35/35 |
| `f_fmamax` | 88 | 96 / 176 B | +3.4 % | +41.99 % | 1/35 |
| `s_splitacc` | 160 | 89 / 288 B | +10.0 % | +6.78 % | 1/35 |

A 45 percent cut in AIR floating-point operations produced a 42 percent
slowdown. The cause is that the Metal backend already contracts `a*b+c`: base
ISA 8,228 B against 8,244 B for the explicit-FMA rewrite, so the 30 percent AIR
reduction never existed in the machine code. This retro-explains the withdrawn
`-ffast-math` control and refutes his own earlier working hypothesis of
floating-point issue saturation.

**Campaign rule 36, credited to alphonse.** Stop using AIR instruction counts
as a cost model for these kernels. Use compiled ISA text bytes and spill bytes
from `research/agx_crossarch.py`. On the three spill-free NA=5 points the
correlation between ISA text and time is near exact.

`n_nosums` at -4.47 percent is the only mover and it is unreachable: it drops
the affine bias-sum term, and `quantized.cpp:1042` already places the `sums`
accumulation in the `m` loop rather than the `r` row loop, so there is no
redundancy to remove. `quantized.cpp:1040` pins the expression tree and any
reassociation changes bits. **Treat -4.5 percent as an unreachable ceiling on
the whole arithmetic axis.**

The pure-load arm is flat in NA, 1.127x over NA=2..6 against 1.804x for the
full kernel. The loads were never the constraint.

NA=5 by more than 3 percent" should count `n_nosums` at -4.47 percent and
`s_splitacc` at +6.78 percent, which move it but are not bit exact. His reading
is correct and I confirmed it in the E108 brief: a fix arm is one that could
legally ship, and an arm that changes the emitted bits is a diagnostic rather
than a candidate. He reported both numbers in full and used `n_nosums` as a
ceiling. The decision does not change.

### (C) Rule 36b - when ISA text ranks arms, and when it lies

Thorfinn's isolated arm table, session s3, 24 blocks, palindrome slot order,
entry 35.72 C, exit 49.49 C, K=5120, N=98336, 157,337,600 B:

| arm | µs | vs shipped | ISA text g16s | delta text |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `a_shipped` | 967.15 | 0 | 3,496 B | 0 |
| `b_constw`, arithmetic only | 960.79 | -0.66 % | 3,696 B | +5.72 % |
| `c_loadonly` | 613.67 | -36.55 % | 1,444 B | -58.70 % |
| `b2_maskalu` | 568.51 | **-41.22 %** | 3,600 B | **+2.97 %** |
| `f_mask` | 616.50 | **-36.26 %** | 3,366 B | **-3.72 %** |
| `h_split`, `g_bfe`, `i_h_unroll` | 967.42 | +0.03 % | 3,490 B | -0.17 % |
| `j_f_nounroll` | 966.9 | -36.24 % | 3,366 B | -3.72 % |
| `e_floor` | 196.54 | -79.68 % | 1,332 B | -61.90 % |

The roofline closes to within 6 µs. `a_shipped = max(ALU 960.8, load 613.7)`, so
the shipped kernel is **issue rate bound** with about 412 µs of load traffic
completely hidden behind arithmetic. `f_mask = max(568.5, 613.7)`, so the arm
becomes bandwidth bound.

**Rule 36b.** ISA text bytes and spill rank arms correctly when an arm adds or
removes work **at a fixed extraction scheme**. They fail when **the extraction
scheme itself changes at constant text size**. `f_mask` was mispriced 9.7x and
`b2_maskalu` had the wrong sign. Whenever the extraction scheme changes, a
measured roofline pair is mandatory: a constant-weight arm that removes the
stream and leaves the arithmetic, and a load-only arm that removes the
arithmetic and leaves the loads. Only that pair predicted the 36 % effect.

Arm B is a static null. `h_split`, `g_bfe` and `i_h_unroll` compile
byte-identical, `efc0d2eb` on g16s and `6ff3d13c` on g17s, so a 64-bit shift does
not cost two instructions on this toolchain. `j_f_nounroll` is text-identical to
`f_mask` and lands within 0.13 µs, so unrolling is not the confound. Spill was
0 B in every arm on both architectures. All full arms were bit-exact across
98,336 rows, and the positive control moved the error from 2.337e-3 to 4.693e-1.

### (D) E108 - a clean null on instruction-fetch footprint, and rule 36c

Merged at `05321b0f`. W&B `75vv3gxq`, `inclcnw4`, `ibpb7lk6`, `typnbamk`, and
`fggmo0zr` which failed on an artifact basename collision and was replaced.

40 scored cells, 5 shapes by M=1..8, 9 blocks per cell, block 0 dropped because
its first slot carried a +144 % median clock-ramp penalty, palindrome slot order,
one ungated counterbalanced session.

| arm | bytes removed | pooled median vs `a_base` | 20k bootstrap CI |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| `h_prunenarrow` | 47,794 B, 38.21 % | +0.019 % | [-0.015, +0.058] |
| `i_pruneall` | 53,604 B, 42.85 % | **+0.003 %** | [-0.015, +0.073] |
| `i_pruneall_null`, comment only | 0 B | **+0.049 %** | [+0.005, +0.080] |
| `a_base_null`, comment only | 0 B | +0.019 % | [-0.006, +0.054] |

Both real prune arms read **below the instrument's own zero point**. No cell
exceeded 1.0 %, the largest single cell was +0.486 %, and there was no monotone
ordering in removed bytes.

**Rule 36c.** Compiled ISA text bytes predict time only through the **executed
body**. Total entry-point footprint is not a cost on Apple family 9. The
literature contains no prior isolation of kernel binary size from executed
instruction count on any GPU, so this null is a first measurement rather than a
replication.

Correctness ran 56 comparisons per arm over 7 widths by M=1..8. The mandatory
control `p_nofallback5` fired with perfect specificity, 7 of 56, always at M=5,
100 % of rows, and nowhere else. `p_misprune5` was bit-identical everywhere,
which proves the generic `qmv_fast_impl` fallback matches the crossrow kernels
bit for bit on every scored shape and width; a mis-prune is visible only in time,
at roughly +34 % at M=5.

**The unplanned second finding.** `i_minus_case5` is the only case whose removal
changes register allocation: 95 to 94 on g16s, and **98 to 91 on the ranked
g17s**. Metal allocates registers once per entry point, so wide case 5 alone sets
a +7 register ceiling for **every** width on the ranked GPU. Under the E77 law
`S_ranked(R) = floor(496 KiB / (128 R))` that is 40 occupants at R=98 and 43 at
R=91, and E102 measured that step at about **+0.1068 %** on G=1 prompts. It is
above the 0.0106 % floor and below the 0.20 % bar on its own, and it is invisible
on g16s because 95 to 94 leaves `S_local` at 32. It cannot be validated locally,
so it is folded into E110 as a rider to price rather than a separate assignment.

### (E) The headline measurement - the one-group rate is 66 % of DRAM peak

Edward and askeladd censused the current tree with two different instruments and
agree to 0.4 pp. All four clean streaming families now run at **65.5 to 66.0 %**
of the 273 GB/s DRAM peak. Before E100 they ran at 99.8 %.

```
14.4123 GB at the measured 179.9 GB/s  =  80,113 us
14.4123 GB at             272.5 GB/s   =  52,889 us
                                          --------
                                          27,224 us = 26.5 % of the 102,864 us M=5 round
```

That is nine times edward's N=5120 anomaly and about 130 times the promotion bar.
Evidence: edward `l8d8golo`, `01djm00q`, `21tw7w2s` at 65.9 %; askeladd
`lzhvble3` at 65.5 % for `lm_head`.

**This is not a regression.** E100 traded two streams at 99.8 % for one stream at
66 % and won 18.4 % of the round. The number is exactly the
`A_local(M=5) = 272.5 / 179.9 = 1.515` that E104 measured at 1.577 isolated and
1.519 in situ.

The source-level mechanism, verified at `quantized.h:969-1063`, per simdgroup per
512-element k-block:

| stream | bytes per simdgroup per k-block | access pattern |
|---|--:|---|
| weights | 4 rows x 512 x 0.5 = **1,024 B** | 8 B per lane, contiguous across lanes |
| scales and biases | 16 B | one pair per row per group |
| activations | NA x 512 x 2 = **NA x 1,024 B** | stride-16-element gather |

Activation load volume is **exactly NA times** weight load volume. At NA=5 the
kernel issues 5 B of activation load for every 1 B of weight load, and the
activation load is the badly shaped one. At fixed `i`, 32 lanes read 4 contiguous
elements each at element stride 16, spanning 1,024 B while using 256 B. The
activation working set is `NA * K * 2`, which is 10,240 B at NA=1 and 51,200 B at
NA=5. Apple L1 is 12 KB per core on families 7 and 8 and undocumented for family
9. 10 KB fits and 51 KB does not.

`group_dims(bk, 2, 1)` is 64 threads, which is two simdgroups. Their `out_row`
differs by `simd_gid * 4`, but they sweep the same k range with the same
activations, so **every activation byte is fetched at least twice per
threadgroup today**. Threadgroup staging halves that before any cache effect.

The occupancy explanation is near-refuted and was pre-registered as such: NA=3 to

predicts +0.042 %, while the measured one-group rate falls 192.7 to 167.1 GB/s,
which is -13.3 %, or 300 times larger than the law allows.

### (F) FINDING 40 - the affine-4 bias may be losslessly reducible to one byte

A board-mining pass over 998 rival submission refs and 1,022 board rows returned
one large untried mechanism, two cheap untried mechanisms, and a long tail of
nulls.

The large one reopens something we parked ourselves. This ledger at
`:14490-14495` says metadata is 11.11 % of quantized bytes at group 64, that
halving it is worth more than any relayout, that every route to halving it
changes dequantized values, and that "only a lossless recoding would qualify, and
that requires the checkpoint's (scale, bias) pairs to have low cardinality".

The cardinality assumption was the blocker, and there is a route that does not
need it. The MLX affine quantizer chooses an integer `q0`, replaces the scale by
`edge / q0`, and stores `bias = edge`. If that construction holds for this
checkpoint then

```text
bias == bfloat16(-z * scale)   for a unique integer z in [0, 16),
                               up to at most one BF16 ordinal of correction
```

so four bits of `z` plus two bits of correction reproduce the stored BF16 bias
**bit for bit**. That is lossless, so it passes the exact-token gate by
construction rather than by measurement.

| record | bytes per 64-element group | bytes per element |
|---|--:|--:|
| shipped | 32 + 2 + 2 = **36** | 0.562500 |
| Bias6 | 32 + 2 + 1 = **35** | 0.546875 |
| bias removed, ceiling | 32 + 2 = **34** | 0.531250 |

| lever | stream cut | local round | ranked at the FINDING 35 factor 0.95 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Bias6 | 2.778 % | **2.461 %** | **2.338 %** |
| whole bias axis, ceiling | 5.556 % | 4.922 % | 4.676 % |

Cross-checked against measured bandwidth rather than share arithmetic: the trunk
streams 14,412,349,440 B per pass, Bias6 removes 400,343,040 B, and at the
measured one-group rate of 179.9 GB/s those bytes cost 2,225 µs against the
102,864 µs round, which is **2.16 %**. The two routes agree, and the lever is
about eleven times the promotion bar.

Board evidence, read through `research/board_prompt_instrument.py`:

| transition | TARGET, plutarch | DRAFT, five G=2 prompts |
|---|--:|--:|
| `902e2026` to `05b6322f`, added | **+0.4069 % (+9.44 sigma)** | -1.1234 |
| `439fc879` to `eff9348d`, removed | **-0.2973 % (-6.90 sigma)** | -1.0861 |

The TARGET probe reverses with the mechanism. The DRAFT probe moves the same way
in both directions, so its movement is residue, not mechanism. Both Bias6 runs
are rank 1 and rank 2 of the 96-run frontier cohort on the TARGET probe, 0.115 %
clear of rank 3, and within newjordan's own 11 schedule-matched runs they sit at
z = +6.13 against controls with sd 0.051.

**Two honest weaknesses, recorded so nobody over-reads the receipts.** First,
their route fires only at M=3..9. Plutarch drafts 38 of 487 rounds, so drafting
is about 14 % of its leg, and 2.78 % on 14 % predicts 0.39 %, against 0.31 %
observed, which is consistent. But the same arithmetic predicts about +2.5 % on
the five G=2 prompts that draft almost every round, and the DRAFT probe measured
-1.12 %. Their consistency check fails by more than 3 pp on the prompts that
score. Second, their routing table sets M=5 to IPG=3, which is the pre-E100
two-group partition; we ship the one-group collapse and must keep it.

**The risk that decides the experiment.** The wide QMV at M=5 runs at 179.9 GB/s,
which is 66 % of peak. If it is bandwidth bound with a shaping problem, removing
2.78 % of the bytes removes about 2.78 % of the time. If it is issue rate bound,
as thorfinn proved the affine-2 kernel is in section (C) above, removing bytes
saves nothing and reconstruction makes it worse, because a 1-byte load and a
2-byte load are the same single instruction while reconstruction adds a shift, a
mask, an integer add and an `as_type`.

Assigned to thorfinn as E111, PR #113, with a zero-GPU numpy rung 0 that either
unlocks or kills the direction in minutes, and a rung 1 whose headline statistic
is the `a_shipped` minus `n_nobias` gap, the absolute ceiling of the whole bias
axis. Kill at a gap below 1.2 %.

collinear fit left `F` unidentified. It does not. With `t = B / 23040` the model
is `us = F + alpha B + beta t = F + (alpha + beta/23040) B`, so OLS returns the
intercept unchanged and conflates the two work terms into one slope. **`S` is the
unidentified parameter, not `F`.** Using askeladd's 1.70 ns per threadgroup ramp,
the ramp contributes 73.8 µs/GB of edward's fitted 5,560 µs/GB, which is 1.3 %,
so `S = 179.9 GB/s` and the 65.9 % result are not collinearity artefacts. The
real limitation is that `F` is identified only under an untestable
linearity-in-N assumption, and curvature lands in the intercept. My separate
conclusion stands: nobody may price a mechanism off that intercept. Note also
that edward's `F = 25.94 µs` is a command-buffer boundary under
`MLX_E58_BUFFER_LIMIT_OPS=0` with one dispatch per buffer and no overlap, while
askeladd's 1.05 µs is the marginal cost of a dispatch inside a packed buffer on
the MTP pass. Two different boundaries, neither substitutable.

### (G) The `xv4` arm. A bit-exact vectorised activation load I sent to alphonse.

Reading `quantized.h:1015-1051` again after his AIR census, the shipped
`DIRECT_NIBBLES = true` branch reads the four activations as **four separate
scalar accesses** `xm[0] xm[1] xm[2] xm[3]`, while the `else` branch calls
`load_vector<T, float, 4, 4>`. His census records the asymmetry directly: **4
activation device loads per k-block body against 3 weight-side**, because the
weight side's `for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) packed[r][i] = ws[i]` folds into one
8-byte load and the activation side does not.

Executed count at NA=5 per lane per k-block: 4 x 4 x 5 = **80 scalar activation
loads**, against about 320 scalar FMAs and 80 conversions. One `vec<T, 4>` load
per `(m, i)` cuts `16*NA` to `4*NA`, so 80 to 20, about 12 % of the issue slots.

**Bit exact by construction:** the same four raw bf16 values feed the same four
conversions into `xc[]` and the same BF16 addition tree into `sums[m]`, with no
reassociation, and fast math is off at `device.cpp:631`. **Alignment proof:** the
element offset is `(first_m + m) * in_vec_size + k + simd_lid * 16 + 4 * i`;
`in_vec_size` in the scored set is 5120, 6144 or 17408, all multiples of 4; `k`
steps by 512. So the offset is always a multiple of 4 elements, that is 8 bytes,
and MLX buffers are at least 16-byte aligned.

The three arms now discriminate rather than guess:

|---|---|---|
| `xv4` | activation issue count | bytes, conversions, registers, address order |
| `mo_swap` | address interleaving and register pressure | issue count, conversions |

| `b_constw` | weight stream removed (WITHDRAWN, see below) | 4 | -0.601 | -0.527 |
| **`e_bias6`** | **the real mechanism** | 35 | **-3.339** | **-2.928** |

NA=4 484.5 / 206.9 / 75.8; NA=5 577.9 / 173.5 / 63.6. Ten sessions, three shapes, four widths;
`e_bias6` negative in nine of ten.

### 258.2 FINDING 43 — THE COST OF THE AFFINE-4 METADATA IS ITS LOAD INSTRUCTION, NOT ITS BYTES

The generation-robust form of the kill, which needs no ceiling estimate and no transfer model:

```
whole 2-byte bias load, measured   = n_nobias - n_nosums  = +2.262 %
exact reconstruction, measured     = e_bias6  - d_bias1   = -2.970 pp
absolute ceiling of ANY lossless recoding of this field   = -0.708 %
```

Narrowing the load from 2 bytes to 1 measures as **nothing**. The reconstruction costs more than
deleting the bias entirely would ever save. That bound uses only differences measured on one host,
so it does not depend on how much of the load cost is bytes and it does not care whether the ranked
M5 is more bandwidth bound than the M4 Pro.

**This closes the metadata-traffic direction, and it closes more than the bias.** The scale field
has the same 2-byte width and the same per-row load structure, so the same result applies to it.
The ledger 14490-14495 estimate that halving all metadata was worth "at most ~5.5 % of the weight
stream" is retired: **no recoding of either field can pay unless it also removes a load.**

My reconstruction-cost warning in `e111-f1` was directionally right and slightly low. I predicted
24-32 reconstruction instructions against 320 of body at NA=4, so 8-13 %. The ISA text says +416 B
against `d_bias1` on the ranked generation at NA=4, about +6 %, and the measured penalty is 2.83 pp.

+509.6 us (+0.287 %) — **because `d4` is a one-bar effect and the instrument cannot see one bar.**
That is the cleanest possible statement of the campaign's measurement problem.

**The variance decomposition is the finding:**

| component | value | share of pair variance |
|---|---:|---:|
| within-leg, after round pairing | 145 us SEM over 76 rounds | **2.1 %** |
| **per-leg (per-process) offset** | **697 us sigma** | **97.9 %** |

Round pairing worked exactly as pre-registered: raw per-round SD 24,377 us, paired 1,266 us,
SEM 145 us = 0.082 % of the round, already under the bar. The floor is not round noise.

**ADVISOR ERROR 67. The offset is not thermal, and my E105 steer was wrong.** I told the team a
tight entry-temperature spread was the route to a usable end-to-end instrument. askeladd cut the
spread from E105's 16.34 C to **3.30 C**, a 5x improvement, and measured:

```
leg offset SD                 520 us
slope vs entry temperature    -47 us/C     r = -0.063    r2 = 0.004
residual after removing T     519 us
```

Temperature explains **0.4 %** of the leg offset. Entry-temperature discipline stays — the official
runner gates on it and a wide spread can still bias a monotone-drift design — but it is not the
resolution lever and I will stop presenting it as one.

**Cost of the instrument we have (design C):** 32 blocks / 128 legs / 3.28 h to halve to 0.235 %;
45 blocks / 180 legs / **4.62 h** to reach the 0.20 % bar on a four-arm decision; 2.31 h for two
arms. That is the honest price of an end-to-end promotion decision in this campaign today, and it
is why so much of our evidence is isolated-harness evidence with a modelled transfer.

**The proposed fix, pre-registered before building.** Alternate the two conditions between rounds
inside one leg. From this session's data, restricted to the dominant `effective_draft_length = 7`
stratum (56 of 77 rounds): round SD 1,020 us, consecutive-round paired diff SD 846 us over 28 pairs,
one-leg SEM 160 us, **predicted one-leg 95 % half-width 313 us = 0.176 %**. The consecutive-round
difference is below `sqrt(2) x 1,020 = 1,443`, so adjacent rounds are positively correlated and
differencing removes slow drift as well as the process offset. That is a **~180x** cost reduction,
1 leg against 180. If the measured one-leg half-width lands near 833 us instead, the diagnosis is
wrong and he says so.

**I have made v2 his terminal deliverable and told him it is the campaign critical path**, with
three riders: state the reachable-arm scope explicitly (within-leg alternation only reaches
conditions switchable per round from Swift, so it serves Edward's Q2 `asyncEval` arm and every
schedule arm but almost certainly cannot serve a Metal kernel-source arm whose name is built by
trusted code at `quantized.cpp:263-273`); test the zero-cost fallback of halving tokens per leg and
doubling leg count, which buys `sqrt(2)` at equal wall clock if the offsets are exchangeable; and
settle exchangeable-vs-drift by regressing the 36 leg offsets on leg order, which is zero GPU on
data he already has.

signature of a rolled loop, not of a cheaper loop.* With `m` outer and `i` inner, `partial[r][m]`
and `sums[m]` become dynamically indexed, the backend declines to unroll the `m` loop, and the four
nibble extractions of `packed[r][i]` can no longer be hoisted across it. Extraction work goes from

branches each, 7 device loads each. Only the AGX machine text separates them and only the clock
decides.

They are never a ranking.** `mo_stage` tracks `mo_swap` to within 2 pp at every width, which
confirms it inherits the same defect. Both are dropped.

The surviving part of my hypothesis is the nibble-extraction hoist, not the nest order. alphonse's
`mo_hoist` keeps the shipped `i`-outer nest and hoists the extraction into `n0..n3[rows_per_simd]`
before the `m` loop. Falsifiable prediction I gave him: if the session-A penalty is really
`16 -> 16*NA` redundant extraction, `mo_hoist` should be neutral at NA=2 and gain with NA. A real
gain at NA=4 means the backend was **not** hoisting and we have a second issue-count lever; flat
means the backend already does it and the axis is closed.

### 258.11 FINDING 45 — E100 MOVED THE QMV GROUP BOUNDARY AND NOTHING IN THE SCHEDULE WAS REFIT

Verified at `quantized.h:1918-1979` on the current base:

| M | instantiation | G |
|--:|---|--:|
| 2 | `<T, 2, 2, true>` | 1 |
| 3 | `<T, 3, 3, true>` | 1 |
| 4 | `<T, 4, 4, true>` | 1 |
| **5** | **`<T, 5, 5, true>`** | **1** |
| 6 | `<T, 6, 3, true>` | **2** |
| 7 | `<T, 7, 4, true>` | 2 |
| 8 | `<T, 8, 4, true>` | 2 |
| 9 | `<T, 9, 3, true>` | 3 |

Before E100, `M = 5` was `<T, 5, 3, true>` and `G` went `1 -> 2` at width 5. **It now goes
`1 -> 2` at width 6.** Cost of that boundary on the current tree, from Edward's E106 census:

```
M=2  78,208     M=5 113,710     M=6 133,564     M=7 144,139     M=8 156,950
marginal:  11,834 per step over M=2..5   |   19,854 into M=6   |   10,575   |   12,811
measured tier ratio at the boundary = 19,854 / 11,750 = 1.69   (E56 fitted 2.0301 one width lower)
```

The schedule prices every step identically. `Qwen36MTPBlockSession.swift:991`
`depthPriceArm = .ship`; `:871-879` `makeUniformDepthPrice()` returns
`marginal[d] = headStepCostRatio = 0.18` for every `d`; `:1040-1112` `costModelDepth()` walks depth
greedily one step at a time. **It charges 1.00x for a step that costs 1.69x.**

Two defects, one family. **D1** the price is uniform. **D2**, the more interesting one, the rule is
greedy on a non-convex curve: the marginal sequence `11,834, 11,834, 11,834, 19,854, 10,575, 12,811`
rises at the boundary and falls back, and a greedy one-step rule will refuse a step whose own
marginal is expensive even when the block behind it is cheap. Fixing D1 alone makes D2 worse.

My rough cost-per-emitted-token pass, to be falsified at rung 0, shows a **consistent bump at
`d5 = M6`, exactly the boundary, that recovers by `d6`** — the right policy is not "stop at 5", it
is "do not stop at 6":

```
beagle, accept 0.834    d3 32,761  d4 31,644  d5 33,417  d7 34,015   optimum d4 (M=5, top of G=1)
essays, accept 0.8974   d4 27,913  d5 28,687  d6 27,837  d7 27,795   flat, bump at d5
botany, accept 0.8655   d4 29,734  d5 30,457  d6 29,591  d7 29,661   flat, bump at d5
```

**Why this transfers when `pbfit` did not.** The source comment at `:985-991` records that `pbfit`
won -3.5 % locally and lost the whole win on the crown table, +0.33 %, a +3.8 pp interaction.
`pbfit` is an 8-parameter shape fitted to one host's measured dispatch times. `pb6` is a one-bit
structural fact about **our own switch statement**, which ships in the archive, so the ranked M5
executes the same partition. FACT 7 adds that `get_qmv_batch_limit` branches only on
`arch_gen == 13 || 14`, so the host-side batch limit cannot move the boundary between gen 16 and
gen 17 either. What can differ between generations is the **size** of the step, not its **location**.

`makeBoundaryDepthPrice(enteringVerifyWidth:)` at `:882-895` is already general and already selects
index `width - 2`, which for width 6 is index 4, the step from depth 4 to depth 5 entering verify
width 6. **Only the enum case is missing. `pb6` is a two-line change.** With E56's factor it gives
`within = 8*0.18/(7+2.0301) = 0.159468` and `marginal[4] = 0.323735`, making the crossing step about
1.89x harder and every other step about 0.886x easier.

### 259.1 E109 MERGED at `914d697b` — the within-leg instrument works, and it costs 6.1 minutes

askeladd, PR #111, head `0a8ba11e`, `succeeded`. Primary
`e109_single_leg_95pct_half_width_us_on_decode_only_round` 833.5 -> **291.8**, minimize. W&B
`cxcgxud9`, `qksvqf0q`, `rdajl7vy`, `adyv927u`, `6npa8brl`, `ynvztyje`. The earlier set
`mcv008be`, `62lyohxj`, `abgc5jor`, `fxto1t8d`, `dhsxqx1h`, `33xgaja7` is superseded; do not cite it.

`291.8 us` is **0.170 %** of the v2 control round `171,771 us`, against a bar of `355 us` / 0.20 %.
His own prediction was 313 us, so the instrument came in 7 % better than designed. The falsifier at
833 us did not fire; the worst leg read 408.5 us.

The design, in one paragraph. One process. The dose alternates round by round. The endpoint is
`block_request_seconds[i]`, the trusted parent's own per-round wall time, which is decode-only by
construction, so Rule 34 holds with no `wall/rounds` denominator anywhere. Estimator 1 is the mean
over consecutive EQUAL-WIDTH round pairs, phase-locked. Estimator 2 is equal-width DUD/UDU triples
`(x0+x2)/2 - x1`, which cancels linear drift. Arms are `a0`, null, and `v2alt`, dose 4 per layer on
alternate rounds. Three null and three dosed legs from three blocks; block 0 conditions the host and
is excluded; there is no outlier rule.

### 259.2 THE REACHABLE-ARM RULE — and I got the table wrong

This is the operative output of E109 and it is now campaign law.

> v2 reaches exactly those arms that (a) can be switched between two adjacent decode rounds by a
> candidate-side flag, and (b) leave the emitted token stream **and** the per-round
> `effective_draft_lengths` sequence unchanged.

```
Swift-side asyncEval placement, per round                       yes
rollback/repair IMPLEMENTATION that does not change acceptance  yes
head compute SCHEDULING with bit-identical proposals            yes
draft-depth / width SCHEDULE POLICY                             NO  <- my table said yes
head POLICY or truncation policy                                NO  <- my table said yes
Metal kernel-source arm                                         no  (name built by trusted code)
begin()-time warm-up change                                     no  (once per leg)
```

Condition (b) kills a depth arm twice over: pairs and triples only form between adjacent rounds of
EQUAL `effective_draft_length`, and the endpoint is per-round while a depth arm changes
rounds-per-token. I told thorfinn in the E113 brief that v2 could serve his arm class. It cannot.
I withdrew that in writing before he needed it.

**THE THREADGROUP-MEMORY KILL, SOURCED.** `qmv_impl<T, group_size, bits>` at `quantized.h:1188` is
ONE function and every path is selected inside it at runtime: the 2-bit draft readout at `:1908`,
the 4-bit wide switch on `ntg.x` at `:1917` where `_wide` inlines, and the narrow and M=1 paths
below, where `lm_head` at `out_vec_size = 248320` lands. **There is exactly one
`qmv<bfloat16,64,4>` entry point for the whole model.** Metal allocates threadgroup memory
statically per pipeline, so a tile declared in `_wide` is allocated for EVERY `qmv` dispatch. An
isolated probe caps simdgroups at 32/20/16/**12** for NA=2/3/4/5, tile = NA x 1024 B, against
`S_ranked = 40`. By the E77 law `Omega(S) = (32/S)^0.01346`, 40 to 12 costs **+1.63 %** against the
arm's -1.078 %, so the composed result is **+0.55 % SLOWER**. Dropped.

The named rescue is parked, not dead: stage the RAW bf16 activations and convert on read. The tile
halves to 2,560 B at NA=5, the cap rises to 24, the occupancy cost falls to +0.69 % against
-1.078 %, and the net is **-0.39 % FASTER**, bit-identical by construction.

**`xv4` is the promotion candidate: -0.498 % ranked as priced, bit exact.** Registers on g16s and
g17s: `a_base` 70/93/94/95 and 83/90/91/98; `xv4` 66/82/94/93 and 93/89/90/101. Kernel text
4,430/5,670/6,934/8,234 B against `a_base` 4,430/5,682/6,920/8,228, which proves the unroll
survives, and AIR device loads per k-block body drop 7 to 4.

**Discriminator answer: ISSUE-SLOT PRESSURE**, not address streaming and not occupancy. `xv8` marks
the boundary: **8 bytes is the widest activation load that costs no extra liveness.**

### 259.9 CAMPAIGN RULE 38, and HARNESS DEFECT 14

**RULE 38.** Any hand transformation that turns a compiler-visible constant-index access into an
indexed-array access is presumed to remove an unroll and must be measured before it is proposed.
`mo_hoist` at +185.29 % on NA=5 is the case that earned the rule, and it extends ADVISOR ERROR 66
from `mo_swap` to the whole extraction-hoist axis. That axis is now closed.

**HARNESS DEFECT 14.** `senpai/rebuild-and-assert-worker.sh` matches needles with `grep` in BRE
mode. `xm[0]` is therefore the character class `[0]`. **A `--forbid` needle containing an unescaped
bracket is a guard that can never fail.** The fix I asked for is `grep -F` with an explicit
`--regex` opt-in, or failing closed on `[ ] * . \` without `--regex`, plus a positive control that
proves the guard can fire.

There is a second, quieter trap next to it. `research/twin_audit.py` carries one allowlisted
comment-only waiver for `quantized` whose two sha256 pins cover both files' comment streams. Adding
comment lines to `quantized.h` or `mlx-generated/quantized.cpp` de-pins that waiver and the audit
then reports the pre-existing `case 8:` comment divergence as live drift. **Alignment and rationale
comments cannot be added to those two files.** alphonse put his alignment proof in the commit
message of `1f531ce7` instead: element offset `(first_m + m)*in_vec_size + k + simd_lid*16 + 4*i` is
a multiple of 4 elements for every scored `in_vec_size` in `{5120, 6144, 17408}`, which is 8 bytes at
bf16, and MLX buffers are at least 16-byte aligned.

and bias loads index by `simd_lid/4`, so four lanes redundantly issue the same load. One lane loads

`n_nosums` and `g_pack32` across at least two shapes, gate_up and mlp.down. Estimated +0.3 to
+0.5 %. Blocked only by file ownership: alphonse holds `quantized.h`.

knee at NA=4, and the live per-lane float working set is about `13 x NA`, since `acc[4]`,
`partial[4]`, `a0..a3` and `sums` are all `vec<float,NA>` at `quantized.h:968-1066`. Zero GPU first:

existing E110 bit-exact arm corpus. About 16 unclaimed roofline points are on the table, so
