### 268.7 — FINDING 75: the ranked measurement mode is a three-slot round robin

This is the result that changes how the campaign reads every official receipt.

564 rows carrying an absolute mode label, ordered by scoring completion:

| lag | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| r | -0.204 | +0.020 | +0.191 | +0.037 | -0.005 | +0.127 | +0.127 |

P(fast given previous completion fast) 0.602, against P(fast given previous
completion slow) 0.807. Wald-Wolfowitz runs test z = +4.83, anti-persistence.
Hour-of-day and day-of-week give nothing.

Three artefact controls all pass:

1. A placebo contrast carrying mechanism but not mode gives lag-1 **+0.114**,
   the opposite sign. Bursts of similar solver code produce positive short-lag
   correlation, so the "solver burst" explanation for the negative lag-1 is
   refuted.
2. The serial leg is produced by the runner-owned prebuilt baseline workspace
   and contains zero candidate content. Over all 770 rows it shows the same
   signature and more sharply: lag-1 -0.236, lag-2 -0.156, lag-3 **+0.327**,
   lag-4 -0.203, lag-6 +0.236, lag-9 +0.141. No candidate can cause this. It is
   the runner's own structure.
3. Consecutive completions by different solvers: P(same mode) 0.464,
   z = -4.46; at lag 3, P(same) 0.642, z = +3.96.

Slot recovery. Slow counts in consecutive triples run 38/95/25/1 for k = 0/1/2/3
against a binomial 52.5/70.4/31.5/4.7, chi-square 16.8 on 3 df: the
distribution is pulled hard toward exactly one slow per triple. Within-triple
variance over triple-mean variance on the serial index is 0.182 where
independent draws predict 1/3, permutation p = 0.0005. Phase-locked recovery
gives slot 0 at P(slow) 0.503 and slots 1 and 2 at 0.236, chi-square 37.7 on
2 df.

The ranked runner behaves as a pool of three interleaved execution slots, one
of which is in the FACT-2 slow state. Consecutive completions land on different
slots; the same slot recurs every three. P(slow) = 1/3 and P(fast) = 2/3 follow
directly, and the campaign's assumed 0.67 was right for the wrong reason.

The slot that is FACT-2 slow is not detectably slower at serial decode: its own
serial offset is +0.015 +/- 0.009 %, against a between-slot serial sd of
0.064 %.

### 268.8 — FINDINGS 76 to 80: the mode is now measurable and correctable, and not exploitable

**FINDING 76 — an absolute per-row mode classifier exists and is 96.0 %
accurate.** Index = w.y with y_p = 100 ln(mtp seconds per token) and w.1 = 0 so
a uniform host-speed change cancels. Weights, mode flip normalised to 1.000:

```
plut -0.3852  drama +0.0215  travel +0.4945  beagle +0.2068
med  -0.1480  republic -0.0917  essays -0.0041  botany -0.0939
```

Separation 3.39 sd, 3.56 weighted. Bootstrap 2-vs-1 mixture LRT 475.3,
p = 0.005. Agreement with the 80 pairwise ground-truth verdicts is 72/75 =
96.0 %. Per-run measurement noise 0.0817 mode units. P(fast) 0.670, and 0.691
after removing an aliasing artefact; both bracket 2/3.

This does not contradict Finding 71. Finding 71 says no fixed linear contrast
can *cancel* the mode continuously, because the mode's magnitude varies run to
run. Classification is a different and easier task: detect a binary state whose
step is 1.000 against per-run noise of 0.0817, then add back its mean.

**FINDING 77 — nothing observable at submission time predicts the mode.** 54
tests, permutation p values, Benjamini-Hochberg at FDR 0.05. Not the solver,
not surface size, not lines added or deleted, not the realised schedule, not
prefill, not hour or day. Most diagnostically,
`serial_seconds_per_token_mean`, which the candidate cannot cause, sits
+0.0146 +/- 0.0094 % higher on slow rows, t = +1.54, p = 0.12. The runner's
serial speed does not tell you which mode you are in.

Two hits survived BH and both are classifier aliasing, not prediction. Head
`477ba726` slows plutarch by 0.451 %, t = 23.0, which is 80 times the mode's
plutarch effect and completely outside the mode's signature; that mechanism
offset displaces the linear index by +1.38 mode steps and the mixture reads it
as "slow". The bulk head `559b24eb`, n = 380, is clean at t = -0.05. **The
classifier is only valid with head provenance held fixed.**

**FINDING 78 — the mode costs about 0.82 ms per drafting round, and prefill is
untouched.** Prefill moves +0.041 +/- 0.066 ms per leg against a 528.4 ms
prefill while the same pairs lose 90.1 ms on decode; a proportional prefill
shift would be 90 sigma. Coefficient of variation of the normalised penalty
across the seven drafting prompts: 0.103 per drafting round, 0.251 per leg
second, 0.323 per verification row, 0.409 per drafted token. Fitted through the
origin, drafting rounds give R2 = 0.856 and non-drafting rounds give exactly
0.000.

This independently reproduces Finding 72, which fitted 0.803 +/- 0.025 ms per
drafting round from a different estimator on a different sample. Two
independent routes now agree to within 2 %.

plutarch remains a 30 to 50 times outlier under every exposure model: it should
pay 31 to 49 ms and pays 0.97 ms. Its mode-immunity is empirically solid and it
is a valid reference. The mechanism of that immunity is still unexplained.

**FINDING 79 — the re-roll lever is real, and it is forbidden.** Because
consecutive completions land on different slots, P(fast within k) is
0.670 / 0.936 / 0.988 for k = 1/2/3, against 0.670 / 0.891 / 0.964 under
independence, and P(at least one fast in a consecutive triple) is 0.994
observed against 0.971. This is recorded so that nobody re-derives it and is
tempted. See rule 72.

**FINDING 80 — post-hoc mode correction is free and worth 5.8 times.** A slow
run publishes 1.3170 +/- 0.0589 % below the same candidate run fast, over 39
cross-mode pairs. P(slow) = 0.330 gives an expected loss of 0.434 % of
published score per submission, and the sd of the mode contribution to one
ranked score is 0.619 %. Classifying the receipt and adding back 1.317 % drops
residual uncertainty to 0.108 %, a 99.0 % reduction in mode variance.

### 268.10 — FINDING 82: FACT 11 is false, and has been for the whole campaign

FACT 11 said "beagle is the lowest ratio in 178 of 178 runs above 3.2". Over
all 326 frontier rows above 3.2 the lowest-ratio prompt is **plutarch in 320**
and drama in 6. **beagle is never the lowest above 3.2** and is lowest in only
3 of all 770 rows.

What FACT 11 meant, and what is true, is that beagle is the **4th order
statistic — the lower of the two central values — in 326 of 326 frontier rows**,
P = 1.000. The ledger already recorded the correct version elsewhere, at line
4045: "plutarch is the 1st order statistic". The two statements sat in the same
ledger and contradicted each other for many rounds.

FINDING 16 is confirmed exactly. `published = 0.5 raw_beagle +
0.5 min(essays, medicine, republic, botany)` reproduces the published score in
326/326 rows above 3.2 and 734/770 overall, and its implied prompt pair matches
the true central pair in 100 % of frontier rows. The order in the frontier
regime is invariably
`plutarch < drama < travel < beagle < {essays, medicine, republic, botany}`.
Slot 5 is medicine 51 %, essays 41 %, botany 4 %, republic 3 %; in all five
Senpai rows it is essays.

The per-prompt serial numerators are flat to 0.03 % of the mean, so the ratio
order is exactly the inverse of the candidate-time order.

### 268.11 — FINDING 83: the exact marginal weight of each prompt

Marginal value of a 1 % candidate speedup on one prompt, computed by
recomputing the median so re-ordering is handled exactly, over the 326 frontier
rows:

| prompt | mean | median | P(>0) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **beagle** | **+0.4862 %** | +0.4859 | **1.000** |
| medicine | +0.2508 % | 0.1128 | 0.512 |
| essays | +0.1598 % | 0.0000 | 0.411 |
| botany | +0.0124 % | 0 | 0.043 |
| republic | +0.0100 % | 0 | 0.034 |
| **plutarch** | **0.0000 %** | 0 | **0.000** |
| **drama** | **0.0000 %** | 0 | **0.000** |
| **travel** | **0.0000 %** | 0 | **0.000** |
| uniform, all 8 | +1.0101 % | | 1.000 |

Rules for pricing a non-uniform mechanism:

1. beagle carries weight **0.484**, hard and not probabilistic, valid up to
   about a 9 % beagle speedup before beagle leaves the central band. The gap
   from 3rd to 4th is 44.5 %, so nothing below can reach it.
2. Any single one of essays, medicine, republic or botany carries about 0.526
   but saturates almost immediately: the 5th-to-6th gap is a median of 1.15 %
   and a p10 of 0.43 %.
3. All four fast prompts together carry 0.526 with no saturation.
4. plutarch, drama and travel carry **exactly 0.000**. They sit 44 % below the
   central band. A mechanism that only helps those three is worth nothing.
5. Single-prompt weights are sub-additive: they sum to 0.919 against 1.010 for
   a uniform improvement.

**FINDING 84 — draft-path mechanisms are not penalised by their
non-uniformity.** The three prompts a draft-path mechanism cannot help are
exactly the three worth zero. A draft-scaled 1 % saving converts at 0.92 to
0.94 of a uniform 1 % saving. This is a material argument in favour of the
draft-path queue, and it reverses an assumption I have been carrying that
draft-path work is discounted for reaching only part of the prompt pool.

### 268.12 — FINDING 85: the transfer coefficient is a class table, and 0.87 is void

The four values that have been used interchangeably measure three different
physical work classes plus one bad assumption.

| work class | ranked = local x | source | confidence |
|---|--:|---|---|
| draft-path per-draft-step head **bytes** | **0.24**, band 0.237-0.33 | measured, E87 arm C; Finding 13 | +/- 1.5x, one mechanism |
| draft-path **dispatch** / launch-latency deletions | **0.95** in percent, 0.52 in absolute us | measured twice, Finding 35 | good, replicated |
| general per-round **DRAM streaming** | **1.0** in percent | Finding 22 | good |
| **acceptance** loss | **1.0** | token-accounting identity | identity |
| ~~0.87 "physical"~~ | **do not use** | invalid | — |

0.30 and 0.24 were never two numbers: 0.24 reuses Finding 11b's 0.237. The
0.87 figure appears in no ledger line as a measurement; it was inferred from a
ranked-frame bandwidth derivation that used the **M4 Pro** 273 GB/s figure when
Finding 22 measures M5 streaming at 542.8 GB/s. It is wrong by about 2x from
the bandwidth alone. **Anything priced from 0.87 is overpriced by roughly 3x.**

A usage trap that has already cost the campaign once: 0.237 is the
**depth-corrected** coefficient, so its denominator must be a local gain
already restated at ranked draft depth. The uncorrected figure for a raw
local-depth gain is **0.327**. Applying 0.237 to a raw local-depth gain
double-counts the depth correction and understates by about 1.4x. And never
apply a byte coefficient to a dispatch deletion; that exact mistake was 12x
wrong at ledger 30094-30100.

Honestly flagged residual: at matched depth the head costs 1,019 us ranked
against 10,090 us locally, a ratio of 0.101, while the bandwidth ratio is only
2.17x. The remaining factor of about 4.5 is measured but not explained.

### 268.13 — FINDING 86: C2 is dominated by `noislands`, roughly four to one

The precision-island question that blocked C2 is resolved, and the answer is to
run a different mechanism.

`mtp-head.manifest.json` describes an affine-4 group-64 precision-island head,
and the `declared` head is the naive affine-4 g64 round-to-nearest
requantization of `master-bf16` with the islands being master bf16 rows at the
highest-SSE indices. Round-to-nearest quantizing those islands back to affine-4
g64 therefore reproduces the trunk's own rows. **C2-with-RTN is numerically
identical to `noislands` while still paying the island tensors, the
`replaceExactRows` matmul and the `putAlong` scatter.** It is strictly
dominated.

C2 could only earn its keep with a better-than-round-to-nearest quantizer, and
E82 rung 6 already closed that: the best post-hoc affine-4 g64 estimator
measured -0.28 pt, the family removes only 8 to 11 % of reconstruction error
over 6.6 M groups, and no post-hoc group-wise affine-4 g64 estimator can
recover the head's 0.82 pt round-to-nearest loss.

Repriced with the class table, because `noislands` removes bytes **and**
deletes two dispatches per draft step:

| | bytes removed | local gain | ranked at m = 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| `noislands` byte component | 31.47 MB | +0.600 % | +0.142 to +0.196 % |
| `noislands` dispatch residual [INFERRED] | — | +0.304 % | +0.289 % |
| **`noislands` total** | | **+0.904 % measured** | **+0.43 to +0.49 %** |
| C2, keeps both dispatches | 22.61 MB | +0.431 % | +0.10 to +0.14 % |

The apparent wrong sign in E82 route (c) is explained as round-count inflation,
not bytes, and route (c) never tested C2 at all.

`noislands` is a roughly three-line change with a zero-GPU stage 0: byte-compare
an RTN affine-4 g64 quantization of the six island tensors against the trunk
rows at the island indices, and refresh the 537-cell offline acceptance
instrument on the current base. If the refreshed offline acceptance delta is
below -0.21 pt, close both C2 and `noislands`. The island region has changed
since E82's base `2b37fd39`, so a replay is mandatory before promotion.

### 268.14 — Advisor errors 86 to 88

**ADVISOR ERROR 86:** in ledger 267 I wrote that the acceptance break-even
falls to 3.5e-3 "on botany, the deepest median-eligible prompt". **Botany is not
median-eligible.** It is the highest ratio, the 8th order statistic, in 266 of
326 frontier rows, with P(central) = 0.043. The binding constraint is beagle,
P(central) = 1.000, break-even m = 4.9e-3. My figure was over-conservative by
about 40 %, and the unspent acceptance headroom against today's m = 2.266e-4 is
**21.6x, not 15x**. I had the correct order statistics in Finding 69's own
table in the same section and picked the wrong row from it.

**ADVISOR ERROR 87:** I priced C1 and C2 with `0.0815 x bytes% - 206.6 x m`,
treating the 0.0815 head-byte law as a ranked coefficient. It is in **local
candidate-time** units: `research/e87_head.py:53-54` says "percent of candidate
seconds per token" and sources it to route (c), which ran on M4 Pro. Ledger
25412-25413 asserts the opposite and is wrong. The direct empirical test at
ledger 26168-26172 gives realised over predicted = 0.112, consistent with the
0.237 byte transfer and inconsistent with 1.0. **Every ranked price I have
computed from that law is overstated by about four times.** The correct form is
`ranked % = 0.0815 x bytes% x 0.24 - 240 x m`. C1's headline of "+0.92 to
+1.08 % ranked" must be re-derived before C1 is assigned, and C2's "+0.38 to
+0.45 % ranked" was a local number mislabelled as ranked.

**ADVISOR ERROR 88:** I issued rule 67 with an acceptance coefficient of 240,
which is botany's. Botany cannot set the median. The binding coefficient is
beagle's 203. Rule 67 is amended below.

### 268.15 — Rules 69 to 72, and amendments to 67

**RULE 67 (AMENDED).** Apply the acceptance penalty per prompt and then
recompute the median exactly, so re-ordering is handled. If a single
coefficient is unavoidable, use **beagle's 203**, not botany's 240. Botany is
not median-eligible.

**RULE 69 (NEW).** Never price a byte-removal, dispatch-removal or acceptance
mechanism without naming its transfer **class** from the Finding 85 table, and
never mix classes inside one price. The coefficient 0.87 is void. State whether
a local gain is at local or ranked draft depth before applying 0.237 or 0.327.

**RULE 70 (NEW).** plutarch, drama and travel carry exactly zero weight on the
published median in the frontier regime. Never optimise for them and never
count a gain on them toward a ranked prediction. They remain legitimate
measurement instruments; an instrument does not need score weight, it needs
mode-immunity and sensitivity.

**RULE 71 (NEW).** Before calling any single ranked run a regression, classify
its mode and correct it. **Never conclude that a candidate regressed on the
basis of a drop below 1.4 % in one uncorrected ranked run.**

**RULE 72 (NEW).** Timing a submission to land on a fast slot, and re-rolling a
submission to catch one, are both forbidden. Re-rolling is a duplicate
submission, which `program.md` prohibits. Slot timing is exploitation of
measurement structure rather than of the candidate, which is exactly what the
static review's measurement-structure-exploitation gate exists to catch. The
mode is to be **measured and corrected for**, never steered.

**RULE 73 (NEW).** A register and spill census is a cost observation and never
correctness evidence, because it reads whole-function summaries and cannot see
what the compiler keeps live across unrolled copies of a loop. Correctness
comes only from an exactness sweep with positive controls. This is the general
form of Finding 65 and thorfinn wrote it.

### 268.16 — HARNESS DEFECT 24: a general-purpose subagent that spawns helpers fails on exit

Two of three research agents this round terminated with
`RuntimeError: child agent exited with uncollected descendants; it must await
or cancel every spawned task first`. Both had completed their work and written
a full report to scratch before the fault, so nothing was lost, but neither
result was returned through the normal channel and I only found them by
listing the scratch directories.

Mitigations, in order of preference: prefer leaf agents where the task does not
need helpers; when dispatching a general-purpose agent, instruct it explicitly
to await or cancel every task it spawns before returning; and in every case
require the agent to write its report to its scratch directory as it goes,
rather than only in its return value. **Always list the scratch directory of a
failed agent before treating its work as lost.**

38826-38828 silently assumed a head side local to ranked transfer of about 1.0,

(ledger 28601, 28625). It also noted that adopting an unmeasured head transfer
is recorded in this ledger as advisor error 40 at line 28892. Two independent

adjustments follow from findings in this same round.

- Finding 85 records a usage trap: 0.237 is the *depth corrected* coefficient and
  its denominator must be a local gain already restated at ranked draft depth.

  correct multiplier is the uncorrected 0.327. That raises the point estimate to

- The agent's own §4.6 records that the byte model over predicts: arm C priced
  1.874 % by bytes and measured 1.265 %, a realisation ratio of 0.675. Applying
  that discount first gives 1.032 × 0.675 = 0.697 % local and +0.228 % ranked.

Recorded band: **C1b is worth +0.23 % to +0.34 % ranked**, against the ledger's
original +0.92 % to +1.08 %. C1a, the gather pass alone, is worth roughly
+0.15 % to +0.23 %.

**The acceptance budget, corrected again for advisor error 88.** The agent used
Rule 67's pre amendment coefficient of 240, which is botany's. The binding
coefficient is beagle's 203. The budget therefore rises slightly, to 1.1e-3 to
1.7e-3 rather than 1.02e-3 to 1.50e-3. **The kill rule does not move.** The
agent's binding budget of 1.0e-3 remains the right conservative choice, and I

**Advisor error 89: I called the offline falsifier free without checking that it
could run.** It cannot run on the advisor host. There is no MLX python anywhere
on this machine. The 18,092 sample hidden state corpus is not on this machine;
`research/e87_job.sh:9` hard codes thorfinn's home directory and every seed path
in `research/e87-corpus-manifest.json` points there. The cluster tables do not
exist here either. The exact head weights and the declared coarse head do exist
on this Mac, but inside Edward's role tree, not the advisor's. So the screen is
cheap, but it is not free and it is not mine to run. Whether thorfinn's dump
survives is unverified.

**Rule 74.** Before describing an offline screen as free, verify on a named
reachable host that the interpreter, the corpus and every auxiliary table exist.
A screen that needs a re circulated 370 MB corpus, or a GPU re capture of 37
seeds at 512 tokens over two passes, is not free.

**Two design improvements over my ledger spec, both accepted.**

1. Do not add an affine-2 rescore kernel. Feed the N survivors straight into the
   existing `qwen35DraftSelectedAffine4RerankKernel` at `Qwen35.swift:3062-3165`,
   which already gathers arbitrary individual rows by id. It costs 0.33 MB more
   than the affine-2 rescore against 53.7 MB saved, it deletes a whole new kernel
   from the assignment, and it removes the affine-2 approximation so the sketch
   becomes the only remaining approximation. Widening past `TOPK = 32`
   (`:3068`, `static_assert` at `:3076`, lane wise reduction at `:3127-3135`) has
   shipped precedent in `qwen35DraftTop32PartialKernel` `:3327` and
   `qwen35DraftTop32FinalizeKernel` `:3427`.
2. Raise the probe fraction, do not lower it. Once centroids are sketched at
   about 132 bytes, probing more clusters is nearly free: p from 0.25 to 0.40
   costs 0.038 pp of local round time and buys back both the centroid sketch
   recall loss and part of the original probe truncation loss. **This inverts
   queue item C4**, which proposed p from 0.25 down to 0.15. C4 stays valid only
   while the centroid pass still streams 1,600 byte rows.

**The two passes have different error semantics and must be staged.** A gather
pass sketch error is repairable, because any row that survives into the top N is
rescored exactly. A centroid pass sketch error is irreparable: a mis ranked
centroid drops all eight of its rows before any rescore can see them. C1a
therefore runs first with the irreparable channel switched off.

**Which sketch.** The task is maximum inner product search over 98,336 rows with
very unequal row norms, and that framing decides the ranking.

| rank | method | bytes/row | fitting | ships an artifact | verdict |
|---|---|--:|---|---|---|
| 1 | low rank k=128 int8 plus fp16 scale | 130 | deterministic power iteration at warm | no | direct norm preserving inner product estimate; Eckart-Young optimal at fixed rank; bandwidth friendly dense matvec |
| 2 | sign sketch, deterministic Hadamard, S=1024 plus norm | 132 | none | no | simplest kernel, popcount precedent already in file; estimates cosine not inner product, so expect large N; best fallback |
| 3 | product quantization ADC | 64-128 | k-means | no | best literature recall, but the lookup table exceeds threadgroup memory; defer |
| 4 | requantization, 1-bit or coarse group | 640-960 | none | no | capped at 2.5x; arm G already measured the bandwidth loss; do not spend the slot |

The fourth row is the important one. **Requantization has a hard floor of 640
bytes per row because it reduces bits per dimension while keeping D = 5,120.
Sketching reduces the dimension itself, 12.1x at S=1024. Same kernel writing
cost, one fifth of the payoff.** Screen methods 1 and 2 head to head in the same
offline run; the screen is one matmul per arm.

**The kernel must be hand written.** `Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/ops.cpp:4810-4816`
restricts group size to 32, 64 and 128, and `:4818-4823` restricts bits to 2, 3,
4, 5, 6 and 8, so 1-bit is rejected; `quantized.h:30-33`, `:109-112` and
`:573-581` repeat the constraint on the Metal side, and `ops.cpp` is not in
`editablePaths`. Ledger 23066-23069 already recorded this. A hand written kernel
reading its own packed `uint32` buffer bypasses the MLX quantization contract
entirely. Every primitive it needs already ships in `Qwen35.swift`: `popcount`
at `:3599` and `:3624`, a threadgroup `atomic_uint` bitmap over the 12,292 leaf
space at `:3583` with `atomic_fetch_or_explicit` at `:3596-3597`, the monotone
`as_type<uint>` float to uint map at `:3235`, manual `uint32` unpack at
`:3097-3110`, and `simd_sum` at `:3120`.

**The sketch is built where the matrix already exists.** `buildDerivedClusterIndex`
at `Qwen35.swift:4630-4696` already materialises the dequantized 98,336 by 5,120
matrix at `:4651` and then discards it. Warm resident tables are 3.98 MB at
S=256, 7.52 MB at S=512 and 14.60 MB at S=1024, against 157.34 MB of
`_draftHeadW/S/Z` that ledger 38872 records as apparently never read again after
the index is built.

**Pre-registered kill rule, adopted as written.** Metric: Wilson 95 % upper bound
on worst *domain* paired discordance against the shipped scorer, at the chosen
method, sketch size, N and p.

- PASS and build the kernel at an upper bound at or below 3.0e-4, which needs
  zero events on both domains.
- REVISE and re-screen with no GPU in the interval above 3.0e-4 up to 1.0e-3.
  Escalate cheapest first: raise N, then raise p, then raise S or k, then switch
  method.
- KILL the configuration above 1.0e-3.
- KILL C1 entirely if the bound is still above 1.0e-3 at the largest budget that
  keeps at least a four times traffic reduction, meaning 400 bytes per row or
  less.

Decide at **domain** level, never at work level. The pooled corpus of 18,092
gives a Wilson upper bound of 2.12e-4 at zero events; the binding expository
domain at n = 5,816 gives 6.60e-4 and tolerates exactly one event; the smallest
individual work at n = 2,634 cannot certify below 1.46e-3 even at zero events,
so a worst work rule would kill every arm regardless of merit.

**Legality is confirmed by the promoted base's own words.** `Qwen35.swift:4625-4629`
states that the derived index "is a fixed function of the checkpoint, in the same
class as a dequantized weight cache or a shape table". A sketch computed at warm
from pinned tensors is in exactly that class. One genuine ambiguity is flagged
rather than guessed: a low rank basis is a new tensor, one step past the promoted
permutation plus means precedent, and sits near the auxiliary predictor hard fail
at `.github/scripts/run-submission-static-review.sh:446`. Mitigation: derive the
basis deterministically from the pinned weights, never from a seeded PRNG.

**Byte budget is not a constraint.** Growth stands at 101,233 of 262,144 bytes
with 160,911 left; per file `Qwen35.swift` is 214,103 of 524,288. C1 is estimated
at about 14 KB, under nine per cent of the remaining growth. An inline
`metalKernel` needs no generated twin and no metallib rebuild.

**Priority verdict.** With C1 repriced to +0.23 to +0.34 % ranked and requiring
two new hand written kernels plus a widened rerank, and with `noislands`
repriced in section 268.13 to +0.43 to +0.49 % ranked for a roughly three line
deletion, **`noislands` now dominates C1 on both value and cost.** Route B
remains far ahead of both. The queue order for the next free bench is:

1. `noislands`, zero GPU stage 0, three line shippable change.
2. C1 rung 0, the offline screen, once a host with the corpus is identified.
3. C5, the 12,292 to 12,296 centroid table pad, as a bit exact rider — and note
   it is only useful if C1b does *not* land, because C1b replaces that pass.

**Residual risks recorded for whoever runs C1.** The corpus may be gone. Achieved
bandwidth on 132 byte rows is unmeasured and arm G lost 191.8 to 179.1 GB/s from
a milder layout change, so short rows may stream materially worse than 1,600 byte
rows; this is the largest technical uncertainty after recall. MLX-Swift symmetric
eigensolver availability is unverified, with fixed iteration power iteration as
the fallback. Warm graph divergence at `Qwen35.swift:356-363` has already cost
this campaign one promoted candidate, so the sketch dispatch must be proved
reachable from the warm call.

### 269.5 Harness defect 25 — the ABBA rebuild gap is an arm-attached thermal confound

Alphonse's finding, and it is real. In an `A B B A` schedule where each arm
change triggers a rebuild, position 3 is the only position with no rebuild in
front of it to cool the GPU behind. Measured entry temperatures across his eight
legs:

```
base arm   40.18  44.87  44.78  44.76    mean 43.65 C
share arm  44.81  53.00  45.09  52.95    mean 48.96 C
```

**The share arm ran 5.31 C hotter on every replicate, by construction.** The
confound attaches to the arm, not to the position, so position balancing cannot
remove it. Here it ran against the candidate by roughly 0.05 pp, so the true
effect is nearer -0.49 %. Fix: insert a matched idle gap wherever a rebuild does
not occur, in `research/e121_e2e_abba.sh`. An arm pair selected by an
environment variable needs no rebuild at all and can remove this confound by
construction; E124 is instructed to exploit that.

### 269.6 Advisor Error 90 and the F74 correction (PR #121, thorfinn)

at `ce97004f` is `tablePays(n:kBlocks:m:) = m >= 4 && n*kBlocks*m > 100_000`
where `m` is the **total row count**, not the accumulator group width. It
therefore takes the table at M=6 and at M=9, and never discarded the 1,643 us
and 3,088 us I attributed to it. Every number I derived from that claim is void.

additivity holds.** Basis M=3 to [3], M=4 to [4], M=5 to [5]; across 28 cells
measured over predicted reads mean 1.510, median 1.146, minimum 0.509, maximum
4.270. It fails by shape rather than by noise: `lm_head` at M=6 reads 4.27 times
and `gdn.out_proj` at M=9 reads 0.51 times. M=3 is a genuine outlier basis.

| 4 | [4] | 77.78 | +3185 | +3185 | +3185 | +3185 | +3185 |
| 5 | [5] | 89.62 | +4322 | +4322 | +4322 | +4322 | +4322 |
| 6 | [3,3] | 122.59 | +2796 | +2796 | +2796 | +2749 | +2796 |

Every gate form is identical at M >= 4 and all 42 cells pay. The entire gate
question lives at M=3 and is worth +62 us of 68,410, or **0.09 %**. He shipped
`tablePays(m: Int) -> Bool { m >= 4 }` and removed the volume term as
unsupported dead complexity, and recommends against a three-entry M=3 exception.
**Endorsed.** A shape-keyed exception worth 0.09 % is below every measurement
floor we own and is exactly the kind of stale conditional that later cleanup PRs
have to delete.

**Ranked conversion:** `ranked % = wide-QMV round % x 0.577`, where 0.577 is the
wide-QMV leg share 0.6068 times the dispatch-class transfer 0.95. That gives
M=3 0.01 %, M=4 2.36 %, M=5 2.78 %, M=6 1.32 %, M=7 2.37 %, M=8 3.28 %, M=9
1.44 %. **Route B is mode-proof at M=4, 5, 7 and 8 but not at M=6 or M=9.**
Beagle's ranked mean width is 5.382 and it carries median weight 0.484, so the
realised width histogram is a first-order uncertainty and rung 5e is decisive.

### 269.7 F87 — the isolated-to-in-situ over-prediction, and where it lives

Three independent observations inside two hours, all near a factor of two.

| source | prediction | in-situ measurement | ratio |
|---|---|---|--:|
| E118 injection ladder against a real deletion | — | — | **1.66x** |
| E123 census time reconstruction at NA=4 | 55 to 85 % pre-registered | 117.2 % | **2.16x** |
| E121 isolated rung 2 to in-situ rung 3 | -0.888 % leg | -0.436 % leg | **2.04x** |

The standard prediction has two terms:

```
predicted leg effect = (per-cell effect measured in isolation) x (that cell's share of the leg)
```

E116 validated the **share** term directly: wide-QMV share of leg 0.6068,
round-to-leg 1.000, `alpha x beta` = 1.000 [0.963, 1.038]. **Therefore the whole
error lives in the per-cell isolated effect.** That is a sharp, testable
statement and it is the framing given to E125.

The factor is not one number. E123 gives 2.164, 1.116 and 1.420 for the same add
tree at NA=4 depending on which half is deleted, so the factor has structure.

**Campaign consequence.** Thorfinn's Route B headline of +2.5 % ranked is priced
entirely from an isolated per-matvec chained-dispatch probe. Corrected by two it
reads about +1.2 %, which clears parity at +0.53 % but sits below the mode-proof
line at +1.86 %. **The factor decides whether the campaign has a winner or a
coin flip.** Rung 5e is the in-situ measurement and is now the most important
single measurement outstanding.

Candidate explanations handed to E125: cache residency in the isolated frame;
clock state, given harness defects 16 and 19; concurrent co-residency, given F17
and `MTL::DispatchTypeConcurrent`; launched-volume mismatch, given E117's trough
of about -11 % over V in 16,384 to 18,432; and instruction class, given the
2.164 / 1.116 / 1.420 triple. The discriminating design is the same deletion in
three frames: standard isolated, isolated with the weight buffer cycled across
enough distinct allocations to force DRAM streaming, and isolated with a
co-scheduled bandwidth consumer. If either modified frame reproduces the in-situ
effect we gain both the explanation and a corrected screening instrument that
costs minutes instead of hours.

### 269.8 F88 — the MTP head precision islands are present at the live pin

Read directly from the declared head artifact the harness loads, sha256
`559b24ebca354018e4402fdb1f5af1afe5a0721bd2ebf04133500d846f7d5f71`, 427,742,600
bytes, 40 tensors:

| tensor | dtype | shape | bytes |
|---|---|---|--:|
| `precision_islands.q.weight` | BF16 | (1024, 5120) | 10,485,760 |
| `precision_islands.k.weight` | BF16 | (1024, 5120) | 10,485,760 |
| `precision_islands.v.weight` | BF16 | (1024, 5120) | 10,485,760 |
| `precision_islands.q.indices` | I32 | (1024,) | 4,096 |
| `precision_islands.k.indices` | I32 | (1024,) | 4,096 |
| `precision_islands.v.indices` | I32 | (1024,) | 4,096 |
| **total** | | | **31,469,568** |

This removes the largest risk on the `noislands` mechanism. E82 measured the
islands on base `2b37fd39` against a different head and campaign rule 65 forbids
porting an old arm's diff; the artifact is present at the current pin with the
byte counts the mechanism assumes, so E124 re-derives rather than ports.

**A consequence that corrects the byte model.** `kIndices` has 1,024 entries and
`kOutputCount` is 1,024; the same holds for V. So `isCompletePermutation` is
true for both, `installExactQKVRows` takes its fast branch, and **the head's K
and V projections are computed entirely in bf16 today, not affine-4**. Only
1,024 of the 12,288 Q rows are corrected, through a scatter.

| path | with islands | without islands |
|---|--:|--:|
| Q affine-4 pack, 12,288 x 5,120 at 4 bits | ~31.46 MB | — |
| QKV affine-4 pack, 14,336 x 5,120 at 4 bits | — | ~36.70 MB |
| Q island matmul, 1,024 x 5,120 bf16 | 10.49 MB | — |
| K+V dense matmul, 2,048 x 5,120 bf16 | 20.97 MB | — |
| **weights subtotal** | **~62.92 MB** | **~36.70 MB** |

Net saving is therefore about **26.2 MB per proposal step, not 31.47 MB**,
because the affine-4 K and V rows must now be read. Repriced under rule 69:

```
byte component     local 0.600 % x (26.2 / 31.47) = 0.500 %  ->  x 0.24 to 0.327  =  0.120 to 0.163 %
dispatch component local 0.304 %                             ->  x 0.95           =  0.289 %
                                                                 ranked total     =  0.41 to 0.45 %
```

The ledger figure of +0.43 to +0.49 % is superseded by +0.41 to +0.45 %.

### 269.9 F89 — the acceptance kill line for a head-precision deletion

Removing the islands cannot break exactness, because the target verifies every
emitted token and the target is unchanged. Only acceptance and time move. Under
F69 the exchange is exactly one to one and acceptance transfers to the ranked
score at coefficient 1.0, while time transfers at 0.24 to 0.95 by class. At the
current operating point of mean draft length 6.36 and acceptance 0.877:

```
ranked time gain              0.41 to 0.45 %
break-even acceptance loss    0.41 to 0.45 % relative  =  0.36 to 0.39 pt absolute
pre-registered kill line      0.21 pt absolute, about half of break-even
```

The kill line is set at half of break-even because the time gain is a prediction
and the acceptance loss will be a measurement.

**Harness defect 25, diagnosed and fixed by alphonse, is the most valuable thing in the
PR.** `swift build` decides what to compile from file stat, so under `base/share/share/base`
only leg 3 rebuilds, and leg 3 is always the same arm. That is an arm-attached thermal
confound that counterbalancing cannot remove: 11 s of prep against 50 to 53 s, entry 8 C
hotter, and only a rebuilt worker pays first-use Metal JIT. Share ran 5.31 C hotter, hot
legs were 0.072 % slower, so the confound ran against the candidate and the true effect is
nearer -0.49 %. The fix, in `research/e121_e2e_abba.sh`, touches both sources every leg so
every leg pays the same compile and the same JIT, pads with `E121_PREP_FLOOR_SECONDS`, and
prints a per-arm thermal balance report that fires correctly on the known-bad session.
**Every student copies this. Nobody reinvents it.**

explanation, because occupancy is what the arm pays and not what it earns: ungated goes
39 -> 32 simdgroups, gated 39 -> 38, and the gain is arithmetic. He then showed that

### 270.2 FINDING F90 — E121 AND ROUTE B REMOVE THE SAME WORK, AND THE OVERLAP HAS A WIDTH MAP

This is the finding of the cycle and I found it only while writing alphonse's next brief.

The shipped wide QMV now carries `constexpr bool SHARE_SUMS = NA <= 4;`. Each simdgroup
accumulates `sums[m]` for its own half of the m range, then the two simdgroups exchange
through `sums_xchg` with two threadgroup barriers per k-block. **That is the same
activation chunk-sum tree that Route B hoists into a replica kernel.** E121 halves it.
Route B removes all of it.

Thorfinn's 7x7 grid was measured against a base that did not contain E121. His gross
numbers therefore price Route B against a control that no longer exists.

The overlap is not uniform. `SHARE_SUMS` keys off IPG, not M, and the dispatch switch maps
them like this:

| M | IPG (= NA) | shares today | thorfinn ranked % |
| --: | --: | :-: | --: |
| 3 | 3 | yes | 0.01 |
| 4 | 4 | yes | 2.36 |
| **5** | **5** | **no** | **2.78** |
| 6 | 3 | yes | 1.32 |
| 7 | 4 | yes | 2.37 |
| 8 | 4 | yes | 3.28 |
| 9 | 3 | yes | 1.44 |

M=5 is the only wide width that does not share, because the wide helper asserts
`NA <= 5` and alphonse gated the share at `NA <= 4`. So Route B's 6.52 % at M=5 survives
whole, and M=5 sits at beagle's ranked mean width of 5.382 on the prompt that carries
weight 0.484 of the published median.

Worst case at the sharing widths, if the overlap is total, gross drops by the full
1.463 %: M=4 from 5.88 to about 4.4, ranked 2.36 to about 1.77. Round-weighted, Route B
would fall from about +2.5 % ranked to about +1.9 % before the isolated-to-in-situ
correction, and to roughly +1.0 to +1.2 % after it.

**Assigned to alphonse as E126, PR #127.** He measures the overlap directly with three
isolated arms on his own instrument: `share_off`, `share_on`, `sums_free`. The
`sums_free vs share_off` contrast is also a cross-instrument replication of thorfinn's
5.88 %, which is worth having on its own under Rule 62.

### 270.3 FINDING F91 — A TRANSFER FACTOR ABOVE 1, AND IT BELONGS TO ROUTE B

Buried in E123's entry-point census, which askeladd computed and correctly declined to
headline because his kill rule had already fired:

| arm | arch | registers | spill | text | resident simdgroups |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `a_base` | g16s | 94 | 0 | 24942 | 32 |
| `n_nosums` | g16s | 95 | 0 | 22710 | 32 |
| `a_base` | g17s | 101 | 0 | 25898 | 39 |
| `n_nosums` | g17s | 99 | 0 | 23608 | **40** |

Deleting the **whole** sums tree crosses a resident-simdgroup step on the **ranked**
architecture and crosses nothing on the local one. Deleting **half** of it crosses
nothing anywhere, which is consistent with E121 measuring 39 -> 38 for the gated arm.

Every transfer factor in F87 is above 1 in the direction that hurts us. This is the first
one that runs the other way, and Route B is the only mechanism in the campaign that
deletes the whole tree.

There is a second and probably larger version of the same effect. The shipped entry point
inlines every width into one kernel and pays the F66 entry-point occupancy tax. Thorfinn's
replica is a bespoke custom kernel specialised to one width and does not pay it at all.

Requested from thorfinn for zero GPU time: an entry-point census of the replica kernel and
of the consuming QMV body, on both `applegpu_g16s` and `applegpu_g17s`. If the consumer
reaches 40 resident simdgroups on g17s, that is worth more than any other free observation
available to him. Added to askeladd's correction table as a fourth index axis alongside
mechanism class, roofline distance and launched volume.

### 270.4 ADVISOR ERROR 91 — I MERGED AN OVERLAPPING MECHANISM WITHOUT RE-PRICING EITHER SIDE

I have priced Route B at about +2.5 % ranked in every plan for two cycles. I merged E121
this cycle. The two remove the same instructions, and I did not notice until I sat down to
write alphonse's next brief, four mutations later.

The mistake is not the merge. E121 is exact, cheap and measured, and it is worth keeping
whether or not Route B lands. The mistake is that I kept a composition sum on the board —
E121 +0.415, Route B +2.5, `noislands` +0.43, C1 +0.3 — while one pair in that sum shares a
mechanism. A composition sum is a claim about independence, and I never checked it.

**New rule.** Before adding two mechanisms in a plan, name the instructions or bytes each
one removes and show that the two sets are disjoint. If they are not disjoint, the plan
carries the intersection as a subtraction and the experiment that measures the
intersection is scheduled before either mechanism is promoted. See Rule 75.

This also changes how a merge interacts with an in-flight experiment. Merging E121 moved
the control that thorfinn's decisive rung measures against. I have asked him to merge
`3f40d9b0` and re-derive on it rather than port a diff (Rule 65), and to treat the shipped
`SHARE_SUMS` body as the 5e control.

| --- | --- | --- | --: |
| E121 rung 2 to rung 3 | cross-simdgroup sum sharing | **adds** a threadgroup exchange, two barriers per k-block | **2.04** (1.55 re-weighted) |
| E120 rung 5e | hoisted activation sum table | **deletes** per-round arithmetic, adds one table read | **0.763** |

Same host, same fixture, same 512-token window, same realised width histogram, and two
mechanisms that touch the same activation add tree. A constant factor cannot fit both
and neither can a constant offset. Askeladd's Stage 0 model
`isolated x (1/W) x (1/F) x share` cannot be repaired by re-fitting `F`, because `F`
would have to take two values at the same width on the same host.

Askeladd's `W` term collapses to exactly 1.00 in the local frame, because thorfinn
aggregated `E[f(M)]` over the realised histogram rather than evaluating `f(E[M])`. `W`
stays live in the ranked frame only, because the board publishes a per-prompt
`effective_mean_draft_len` and never a per-prompt histogram. The ranked width
distribution is unidentified.

Askeladd's branch R is **void**. Thorfinn's 7x7 grid is indexed by total M with the
shipped partition already applied, which his own numbers prove: the fractional gains
cluster by instances per group and not by M. IPG 3, at M=3, 6 and 9, reads 2.20, 3.30,
3.16. IPG 4, at M=4, 7 and 8, reads 5.88, 4.92, 6.69. IPG 5, at M=5, reads 6.52. The
underlying worry survives in a stronger form: `f(5) = 6.52` against `f(6) = 3.30` is a
factor of 2.0 across the exact width beagle sits on, and beagle carries 0.4862 of the
marginal weight alone.

**Revised E125 Stage 2 deliverable.** Not a scalar and not a single function of phi. A
class-by-regime table, `correction(mechanism class, roofline regime) -> factor` with an
interval, validated against both anchors rather than fitted to them. Added kill rule:
the table must reproduce both 2.04 and 0.763 inside their measured intervals. A table
that fits one and misses the other has picked a side, not explained the phenomenon.

### 271.7 E124 CLOSED — A DUPLICATE OF A CLOSED NEGATIVE

**Advisor error 93.** I assigned E124 from a byte model without reading E82's measured
net. Rule 68 exists for exactly this and I violated its spirit.

E82, `research/e82-artifacts/terminal-result.md`, W&B `o0rawiol` and `yerghmxz`, ran the
same mechanism at 512 tokens, ungated, six-leg palindrome, one M4 Pro session,
`--sync-head`, every leg exact:

| arm | mean s/tok | rounds | delta |
| --- | --: | --: | --: |
| `declared` | 0.031432 | 78 | ref |
| `noislands`, edward's arm `none` | 0.031547 | 79 | **+0.366 %** |
| `qonly`, edward's arm `q` | 0.031998 | 80 | **+1.801 %** |

`max(declared) = 0.031454 < min(noislands) = 0.031538`. Round counts are exactly
reproducible across the palindrome's repeat visits. E82 built separate head artifacts,
so its arm also dropped 31.5 MB of resident memory that edward's env-selected arm still
holds; E82's arm is strictly more favourable and it still lost.

Edward's corrected model reproduces that result:

```
one extra decode round        = 151,471 / 15,694,534 = 0.965 % of the leg
gross saving, arm none        = 0.532 byte + 0.018 dispatch = 0.550 %
net                           = -0.415 %  (slower)
E82 measured                  = +0.366 %  (slower)
model minus measurement       =  0.049 pp
```

The model is validated to five hundredths of a point against an independent 512-token
measurement, and the mechanism is dead: the acceptance repayment is 1.8 times the byte
saving. Arm `kv`, the only arm E82 never ran, can afford 0.220 extra rounds and has a
ceiling of +0.048 to +0.065 % ranked even at zero acceptance cost. It does not justify a
slot.

**The +0.904 % figure in the E124 brief was never a net measurement.** It was E82's
gross head-time component, -57,720 us, before +72,166 us of verify and +46,988 us of
wait for the extra round. Findings 86, 88 and 89 carried a gross number as a net one and
then built a residual dispatch class on top of it.

**Edward's four corrections, all accepted.**

1. The byte model must count scales and biases: 2,880 B per affine-4 g64 row, not 2,560.
2. `appendHistoryKV` at `Qwen35MTP.swift:235` reaches the same island fast branch once
   per round and adds 15.07 MB per round to the saving of arms `none` and `q`.
3. **The 0.304 % dispatch residual is struck.** It was E82's measured 0.904 % local
   minus a 0.600 % byte model, and a residual is not a transfer class. Priced as an
   actual dispatch class it is 19.08 dispatches per round at 1.05 to 1.80 us, which is
   0.013 to 0.023 % local, thirteen times smaller. Queue audit: that residual was used
   only in the `noislands` price. C1 and C5 are priced from counted bytes, C4 was
   measured directly, and Route B and E121 are priced from measured counts. Nothing else
   moves.
4. **The arm ladder is reversed.** Dropping the K and V islands removes more bytes than
   dropping the Q island, and E82 confirms it from the other side: `qonly` was the worst
   arm at +1.801 %. Dense bf16 K and V are worth more acceptance than 1,024 corrected Q
   rows out of 12,288.

Edward finishes Stage 0.5, posts the corpus regime table and goes terminal. He then
takes E127.

### 271.11 HARNESS DEFECTS 26 TO 30

**26.** `yukon submissions` wraps the status field in ANSI colour codes even when piped.
`grep -c promoted` works and `awk '$3 ~ /promoted/'` works, but `grep ' promoted '` and
`awk '$3 == "promoted"'` both return zero. An exact-match parse returns zero rows and
exits cleanly, so a receipt watcher reports "nothing yet" forever.
`research/yukon_receipt_watch.sh` is affected and is not fixed. Strip with
`sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g'` before any field parse and add a positive control line.

**27.** A 64-token or 128-token local window understates a per-round kernel effect by a
large factor, measured at **3.8** between thorfinn's 64-token screen and his 512-token
session on identical code. No short-window screen may be reported as an effect size,
only as a sign test.

**28.** `MLXFAST_*` never reaches a runtime-worker leg.
`sanitizedRuntimeWorkerEnvironment` in
`Sources/MLXFastTrustedHarness/QwenRuntimeWorker.swift` forwards ten exact names plus the
prefixes `DARKBLOOM_ DYLD_ LC_ METAL_ MLX_ MTL_`, and the maintainer contract in that
file forbids adding a broad `MLXFAST_` allowance. Ledger 197(H) already recorded this and
the E124 brief did not carry it. **Campaign audit run this cycle and clean:** the three
dead model-side gates are `MLXFAST_QWEN_MTP_EXACT_QKV_ROWS`, `MLXFAST_QWEN_MTP_TOP32` and
`MLXFAST_QWEN_MTP_TRACE`, and no campaign number depends on any of them. E82 used
separate head artifacts and E122 ran the CLI in process. Use the `DARKBLOOM_` prefix for
any future model-side arm selector, with precedent at
`Qwen36MTPBlockSession.swift:224`. Such a selector must never reach a submitted surface.

**29.** `research/e123_arms.py` does not build against the current base. E121 rung 3
(`5d97175c`) added `uint simd_gid` and `threadgroup float* sums_xchg` to the shipped
`qmv_fast_crossrow_affine4_g64_wide`, so the emitter's per-width entry points now pass 10
arguments to a 12-argument function. Only `a_base` fails, because every other arm
substitutes its own prologue. It is a stop rather than a corruption. Askeladd works
around it by emitting from twins pinned at `5d97175c~1`, byte-verified against
`research/e123-artifacts/meta.txt`.

**30.** The arm palindrome cannot remove the defect-16 clock ramp when the arm set is
short. Each `gpuTempC` call leaves the GPU idle about one second, the following ramp
burst is 150 ms, and the slot sequence inside a block then falls **convexly**. A convex
fall does not cancel: arm 0 pairs the slowest slot with the fastest while the middle arm
pairs two neighbours. Measured forward-minus-reverse residual on a 10 ms smoke block ran
+50.4 % on the end arms down to +11.7 % in the middle, monotone in slot position. At a
real 40 ms window it put `a_base` 12 % above `q_scaffold` on byte-identical sources.
E123 did not see it because 36 arms give a 72-slot 8.6 s block; E125 saw it because 7
arms give a 14-slot 1.7 s block. **Fix:** `--warm-sweep-reps`, default 2, one discarded
arm palindrome per block before the timed one. This should become the default on the
shared instrument.

Askeladd also corrected the residency table I gave him. The +1 simdgroup step exists
only at the **width-0 whole-file entry point**, which is not a kernel that runs. At every
width that does run, deleting the whole add tree **raises** register pressure at NA>=3 on
both architectures, because it removes a serialising dependence chain. At NA=4, the
scored width, g17s **loses** 3 of 44 resident simdgroups and g16s loses none. Axis 3 at

### F100 — THE REGIME VARIABLE IS WHETHER THE REGISTER BUDGET BINDS

F33 and F34 record host register budgets **g16s 96, g17s 124**. F91 records `a_base` at
**94 registers on g16s** and **101 on g17s**, both zero spill.

On g16s the kernel sits 2 registers under a 96-register budget, on the cliff edge, so any
register relief buys occupancy. On g17s the same kernel sits 101 against 124, with 23
registers of slack, so register relief buys nothing and a barrier is pure cost.

**Pre-registered.** E121's local gain is an occupancy gain that exists only where the
register budget binds. On g16s the `SHARE_SUMS` work split relieved pressure at a binding
budget and paid for its two `threadgroup_barrier` per k-block. On g17s there was no
pressure to relieve, so only the barrier and `sums_xchg` exchange cost remained.

**Falsifier.** At NA=5 `SHARE_SUMS` is false, so M=5 pays the extra parameters and the
threadgroup allocation but never the split or the exchange. If F100 holds, the g17s cost is
present at M=6, 7, 8 and absent at M=5. If it is present at M=5, the cause is the
parameters or the allocation instead.

This replaces roofline `phi` as the regime axis for the E125 correction table. It is
testable by census, with no GPU time.

### 🔴 BUT THE ESTIMATOR AXIS IS NOT, AND NOBODY HAS LOOKED AT IT

F97 closes the **price**. It does not close the **reach estimator** that decides how far to
walk under that price. Pricing our realised ranked depths on the fitted curve:

| prompt | p | realised d | us/token realised | us/token at d=7 | gap | x F83 weight |
| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| beagle | 0.9341 | 4.382 | ~11941 | 11640 | **2.52 %** | **+1.23 %** |
| medicine | 0.9639 | 5.256 | ~10868 | 10520 | **3.20 %** | **+0.80 %** |
| essays | 0.9647 | 5.087 | — | — | ~3.4 % | **+0.54 %** |

**A constant-p reading of the gap is worth about +2.6 % on the published median**, larger
than Route B's central ranked estimate, with no kernel work.

The suspect is at `Qwen36MTPBlockSession.swift:1091-1099`. `p = Swift.min(p, conf)` with
`conf = sigmoid(margin/2.0)` at depth 0 and `sigmoid(margin/3.0)` at depth 1 is a **strictly
downward** override that can only shorten a round, and it binds whenever the margin is below
about 5.2. E122 measured the margin's pooled AUC at **0.5109 [0.4850, 0.5364]** over 57,907
pairs, indistinguishable from random — but it measured `benchfixture`, the one in-regime
fixture, at **0.7998**. Pooling destroyed the stratification, so this must be settled per
regime.

The +2.6 % is an **upper bound** under constant p. The real number depends on the uncensored
per-position decline, which the shipped adaptive policy cannot observe because it is
selection biased. E92's per-position conditionals are survivor biased upward and unusable.
A forced-depth-7 arm measures it directly.

### NEW RULES

**Rule 79** — A local timing measurement cannot validate a draft-depth or schedule change.
The ranked cost tier breaks entering width 5 while the post-E100 local dispatch group
boundary breaks entering width 6; the optima disagree in 18.2 % of the plausible acceptance
space and chasing the local optimum costs up to 8.66 % ranked. Price schedule policy on the
board-fitted ranked curve, never on a local ratio.

**Rule 80** — An accept "rate" is not a per-step conditional acceptance probability. Invert
`E[accepted] = p(1-p^d)/(1-p)` before feeding any acceptance number into a depth or schedule
model.

**Rule 81** — Before merging any scored-surface change on a local read, name the ranked
receipt that will confirm it, and do not compose a second mechanism on top until that
receipt lands.

**Rule 76, amended** — The regime variable is the per-step conditional p, not the accept
rate. The median-carrying band is p in [0.934, 0.966]. Stratify, never pool.

### F101 — THE RESIDENCY FLOOR LAW

```
resident simdgroups = floor(REGISTER_BUDGET / registers_per_thread)
REGISTER_BUDGET = 3072 on applegpu_g16s,  3968 on applegpu_g17s
```

Holds **exactly in all 8 census cells on both architectures**. This is not a fitted
relation; it is the allocator. It converts a compile into an exact occupancy reading for
the ranked machine, at zero GPU cost and with no thermal gate.

This retires `phi` and the roofline as the regime axis. `phi` was a proxy for a quantity we
can now compute.

### F102 — THE ENTRY POINT PAYS MAX-OVER-BODIES REGISTER PRESSURE

```
g16s: max(66, 82, 94, 93) = 94    measured entry point = 94    CONFIRMED
g17s: max(93, 89, 90, 101) = 101  thorfinn read incumbent = 101 CONFIRMED, and 3968/101 = 39
```

Every wide-QMV dispatch, at every width, currently runs at the worst width's occupancy. The
`switch` over M compiles to one kernel allocated against NA=5.

Templating per width, priced through F101 and weighted by F47:

```
applegpu_g17s (RANKED)   entry 101 regs -> 39 sg paid at every width
  NA2 body  93 -> 42 sg   +7.69 %   weight 0.024
  NA3 body  89 -> 44 sg  +12.82 %   weight 0.275
  NA4 body  90 -> 44 sg  +12.82 %   weight 0.667
  NA5 body 101 -> 39 sg   +0.00 %   weight 0.034
  F47-weighted: +12.26 %   ->  +1.23 to +3.68 % ranked at 0.10-0.30 %/%

applegpu_g16s (LOCAL)    entry  94 regs -> 32 sg
  NA2  66 -> 46 sg +43.75 % | NA3  82 -> 37 sg +15.62 %
  NA4  94 -> 32 sg  +0.00 % | NA5  93 -> 33 sg  +3.12 %
  F47-weighted:  +5.45 %
```

**On g16s the dominant NA=4 cell IS the register maximum, so templating buys it exactly
zero. On g17s it has eleven registers of slack.** That is why nobody found this locally,
and it is a 2.3x systematic understatement for any local measurement of this arm.

Assigned as **E130, PR #130, alphonse**. This is the largest identified untried lever.

### F103 — THE REGISTER DELTA INVERTS SIGN ACROSS GPU GENERATIONS

```
cell   g16s regs   g16s sg      g17s regs   g17s sg
NA2    66 ->  68   46 -> 45     93 ->  80   42 -> 49
NA3    82 ->  79   37 -> 38     89 ->  95   44 -> 41
NA4    94 ->  90   32 -> 34     90 -> 102   44 -> 38
NA5    93 ->  93   33 -> 33    101 -> 101   39 -> 39
F47-weighted residency:  g16s +4.86 %   g17s -10.57 %
```

The same source moves registers **-4 on g16s and +12 on g17s** at the dominant cell. NA5 is
an exact null on both architectures because `SHARE_SUMS = NA <= 4` is false there, including
identical ISA text sizes (8234/8234 g16s, 8452/8452 g17s). That null is the internal control
that rules out compiler noise, and it is exactly the discriminator alphonse pre-registered.

**F100 is confirmed and upgraded.** The regime variable is the register budget, and the cost
is the split and the exchange, not the extra parameters and not the threadgroup allocation.

The residency coefficient brackets from two confounded points:

```
g16s:  +4.86 % residency, +1.463 % kernel gain  -> 0.301 %/%  (LOWER bound; E121 also added barriers)
g17s: -10.57 % residency, +2.10 % ranked loss   -> 0.199 %/%  (UPPER bound; same confound, opposite sign)
```

E130 rung 2 attacks this with a regression discontinuity: the floor law is a step function,
so a register ladder walking through a step separates occupancy from instruction count. If
time moves only at the crossings, occupancy is causal. If it moves smoothly, my pricing
model dies and the axis closes again.

### F104 — THE RANKED ROUND COUNT R IS UNPUBLISHED, UNPINNED, AND PROBABLY WRONG

I stress-tested the +2.6 % E128 estimate. It survived every shape test. Then I checked its
input and the input is an assumption.

Published per-prompt fields are exactly `accepted_pair_count`, `effective_mean_draft_len`,
`head_provenance_sha256`, `mtp_seconds_per_token_mean`, `non_drafting_round_count`,
`noop_reference_decode_speedup`, `parity_ok`, `prefill_seconds_per_token`, `prompt_sha256`,
`raw_ratio_of_means`, `serial_seconds_per_token_mean`.

Three traps, all of which I walked into:

- `accepted_pair_count` is **1** on every prompt of every receipt. It is the thermal pair
  count, not a round count. A calibration script built on it produced -99 % errors.
- `noop_reference_decode_speedup` is **exactly 1** everywhere, consistent with `program.md`
  saying there is no no-op normalization. It is not an anchor.
- `non_drafting_round_count` is **0** on all seven drafting prompts and **449** on plutarch.

The accounting leaves R free:

```
R = 512 - A,   A = R * eff * accept_rate   =>   accept_rate = (512 - R) / (R * eff)
```

Two unknowns, one equation. `research/rankedcurve.py` hardcodes an assumed vector under a
"maximal-tokens-per-round rule". **F12, F92's accept rates, the fitted ranked cost curve,
F97, and my +2.6 % all inherit it.**

**It is arithmetically infeasible.** The shipped `costModelDepth` with the uniform 0.18 price
is a step function of a flat per-position acceptance, with exact thresholds

```
d>=1 at p>0.1800  d>=2 at p>0.4742  d>=3 at p>0.6497  d>=4 at p>0.7527
d>=5 at p>0.8168  d>=6 at p>0.8591  d>=7 at p>0.8884
```

so `E[depth] = sum_k P(p > t_k)`, and the maximum mean `p` compatible with an observed
`E[depth]` is a small LP over the threshold points:

| prompt | eff | assumed R | p from accounting | max feasible E[p] | verdict |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| beagle | 4.3818 | 110 | 0.9335 | 0.8401 | **INFEASIBLE** |
| medicine | 5.2556 | 90 | 0.9637 | 0.8935 | **INFEASIBLE** |
| essays | 5.0870 | 92 | 0.9646 | 0.8832 | **INFEASIBLE** |
| botany | 6.1481 | 81 | 0.9597 | 0.9480 | **INFEASIBLE** |
| republic | 4.9892 | 93 | 0.9661 | 0.8772 | **INFEASIBLE** |
| drama | 2.2976 | 252 | 0.5983 | 0.6803 | feasible |
| travel | 2.6557 | 212 | 0.6960 | 0.7172 | feasible |

**It fails on exactly the five prompts that carry the median and holds on exactly the two
that carry zero weight.** Mechanically: at p = 0.9335 the shipped scheduler runs to the cap
of 7, yet beagle reports a mean of 4.38.

R decides the SIGN of the E128 correction, not just its size:

```
beagle, sweeping R   accept rate  per-step p  optimal d   gain %   direction
      96                0.9889      0.9959        7.0      9.546   DEEPER
     110 (assumed)      0.8340      0.9335        7.0      2.231   DEEPER
     118                0.7620      0.9012        3.0      2.279   SHALLOWER
     150                0.5508      0.7887        3.0      8.715   SHALLOWER
```

Eight rounds of R separate "draft deeper" from "draft shallower". The gain is near zero only
where the observed depth happens to sit at the optimum.

Re-pinning R also moves the fitted cost curve, because `round_us = 512 * mtp_spt / R`. At the
minimum feasible R the deep prompts get 17-20 % cheaper per round and the shallow ones 3-10 %
dearer, so the curve **flattens**. The two effects fight: a flatter curve favours deeper
drafting while a lower acceptance favours shallower. The sign is currently undetermined.

### F105 — THE SCHEDULER'S `expected` IS PROFILE-FREE EQUAL TO THE ACCEPTED-DRAFT COUNT

`reach *= p` then `expected += reach`, so at termination

```
expected = sum_{k=0}^{d-1} prod_{j=0}^{k} p_j  ==  E[accepted drafts this round]
```

identically, with no flatness assumption. Combined with the window accounting:

```
R = 512 / (1 + E[accepted drafts per round])
```

**So the calibration E128 was sent to audit is the same number that pins R.** One measurement
answers both. Implied `E[expected]` under the assumed vector: beagle 3.6545, medicine 4.6889,
essays 4.5652, botany 5.3210, republic 4.5054, drama 1.0317, travel 1.4151, plutarch 0.0513.

Pre-registered falsifier for E128 rung 1, from the stop rule plus monotonicity of `reach`:

```
beagle    R=110 survives ONLY IF geo-mean(p_0..p_3) >= 0.8995 AND p_4 <= 0.7442
medicine  R= 90 survives ONLY IF geo-mean(p_0..p_4) >= 0.9282 AND p_5 <= 0.7823
essays    R= 92 survives ONLY IF geo-mean(p_0..p_4) >= 0.8922 AND p_5 <= 0.9328
```

A flat or slowly-declining profile falsifies the assumed R outright.

Also mechanically explained: `non_drafting_round_count = 0` on all drafting prompts because
the depth-0 threshold is 0.18 while the margin gate floors `p` at `sigmoid(0) = 0.5`. The
depth-0 gate can never fire.

### F109 — PER-WIDTH TEMPLATING IS UNREACHABLE IN `quantized.h` AND FULLY REACHABLE IN `Qwen35.swift`

The incumbent width switch is **inside the kernel** at `quantized.h:1923`, on `ntg.x`. The host
dispatcher that would have to build a per-width kernel name is
`Vendor/mlx-swift/Source/Cmlx/mlx/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp`, which is **not** among
`benchmark.json`'s 89 `editablePaths`. All widths therefore compile into one Metal function, one
pipeline state, one register allocation. That is the mechanism behind F102.

**Route B is different and the difference is decisive.** It builds its own Metal source as a Swift
string and creates its own named kernels:

```
Qwen35.swift:1562  qwen35E120QMVSource(table:)              builds the source
Qwen35.swift:1565  cases = [(3,3),(4,4),(5,5),(6,3),(7,4),(8,4),(9,3)]
Qwen35.swift:1588  switch (qmv_m) { ... }                   a RUNTIME switch we own
Qwen35.swift:1596  MLXFast.metalKernel(name: "qwen35_custom_affine4_g64_qmv_wide_v1", ...)
Qwen35.swift:1605  MLXFast.metalKernel(name: "..._qmv_wide_sums_v1", ...)
Qwen35.swift:1806  template: [("USE_TABLE", consume)]       <- MLX emits one pipeline per tuple
Qwen35.swift:1814  Qwen35CustomQMV.matmul                   the Swift-side dispatcher
```

Adding `("QMV_M", cell.m)` to the template list and replacing the runtime switch with a
compile-time dispatch gives every width its own Metal function, its own register allocation and its
own occupancy, with **an instruction channel of exactly zero** — the emitted code per width is
identical, only the pipeline boundary moves. No other arm on the board reads the residency channel
clean.

Hard gate on that arm: seven widths times two `USE_TABLE` values is up to fourteen pipelines against
one today. Seed processing and decoding are both inside the timed leg, so a first-use JIT compile at
a rare width is paid inside the measurement and on all eight ranked prompts. Zero in-leg pipeline
creations must be **proved**, not assumed.

### F112 — THE REACH ESTIMATOR IS BIASED LOW BY 9 TO 24 %, AND IT IS A LEVEL DEFECT, NOT A DISCRIMINATION DEFECT

Read from the recorded `sched=` walk per round against the realised accepted count, 12 fixtures:

```
fixture           rounds  mean expected  mean accepted   bias %   slope     r
beagle_a             119      2.868          3.303       -13.2    1.037   0.889
beagle_b             126      2.712          3.063       -11.5    1.085   0.909
benchfixture          78      5.067          5.577        -9.2    0.851   0.708
botany_andrews       143      2.149          2.587       -17.0    1.050   0.860
drama_dollhouse       92      3.933          4.565       -13.8    1.019   0.952
essays_bacon         285      0.836          0.797        +5.0    0.512   0.195
essays_montaigne     146      1.906          2.507       -24.0    0.655   0.515
medicine_hippoc       80      4.552          5.400       -15.7    1.018   0.937
medicine_hist        153      2.088          2.346       -11.0    1.060   0.840
plutarch_lives       180      1.533          1.844       -16.9    1.257   0.790
republic_jowett      104      3.377          3.923       -13.9    1.056   0.930
travel_eothen        172      1.786          1.977        -9.7    0.834   0.640
```

Biased low on 11 of 12, slope ~1.0 and `r` 0.86 to 0.95 on every median-regime fixture. **The
estimator ranks rounds correctly and sets its level too low.** The single unbiased fixture,
`essays_bacon`, is also the only one with no discrimination at all.

**HYPOTHESIS J, assigned to E128.** The walk computes `reach = prod_j pbar_j` from global position
EMAs, while the realised count has expectation `E_round[prod_j p_j(round)]`. A product is convex, so
`E[prod] >= prod E[.]` with equality only at zero per-round variance. That predicts a level bias with
slope 1, no loss of ranking, a gap that grows with depth, and its own exception: `essays_bacon` has
mean `expected` 0.836, almost no product to be convex over, and it is exactly where the bias vanishes
and `r` collapses. One mechanism, four predictions.

**The sign of the correction is NOT settled and must not be asserted.** Both biased quantities enter
`guard reach > marginal[d]*(1+expected)/cumulative[d]` on opposite sides: `reach` low drafts
shallower, `expected` low lowers the threshold and drafts deeper, and at `expected ~ 3` the two are
the same order. E128 replays `reach`-only, `expected`-only and both.

Edward's correct objection to my framing: **F97's price optimality was established against the
biased estimator**, and price and estimator enter the same comparison, so they are not separable by
observing depth. Rung 2 sweeps them jointly.

### F114 — THE BANDWIDTH AXIS IS DEAD, AND THE DELETED INSTRUCTION COUNT KILLED IT

Recomputed on the 20 E123 cells:
```
pooled r(gain, bandwidth)                       -0.872
pooled r(gain, residency)                       +0.817
partial r(gain, bandwidth | residency)          -0.787   survives
pooled r(gain, deleted instruction count)       +0.949   <- the strongest correlate
nested r2: instructions alone 0.9014 | + bandwidth +0.011 | + residency +0.006 | both +0.021
width-demeaned r(gain, bandwidth) = -0.485, sign flips -0.972 at NA=3 to +0.874 at NA=5
```
Residency is constant inside every width and cannot explain a within-width correlation. The deleted
instruction count alone explains 90 % of the variance. **This reconciles askeladd's pooled -0.862
with thorfinn's in-situ `r = -0.067, p = 0.855` without either being wrong**: the headline was a
width effect. Thorfinn's refutation stands and is now explained.

Askeladd's Stage 2 class-by-regime correction table **fails its own kill rule at 0 of 2 frame
anchors** and the two-channel law cannot rescue it, because a register count is fixed at compile time
and is therefore identical in the kernel and leg frames on one host — the residency channel is
structurally zero across any within-host frame pair. The composition that survives is
`effect(class, frame, arch) = F(class, frame pair) x [ I(class) + c * R(class, arch) ]`, and `F` must
still be measured. Route B kernel-to-leg is 0.763; E121 kernel-to-leg on g16s is `0.433/1.463 = 0.296`.
**F is class-dependent, not a constant.** F85 and F87 stand.

### NEW RULES

**Rule 85 — Never report a pooled correlation across widths on this kernel.** The width axis moves
the instruction count, the register count and the achieved bandwidth together, so a pooled `r` is a
width effect wearing whichever costume the author reaches for first. Stratify or use a width fixed
effect.

**Rule 86 — Every published price-ladder cell must carry the register delta of both of its rungs.**
A contrast with a non-zero register delta is not an instruction reading and must be labelled as
carrying an occupancy term.

**Rule 87 — Every quoted residency coefficient names its frame.** The entry-point leg frame gives
`c = 0.445 [0.139, 0.819]`; the isolated-body F47-weighted frame gives `c = 0.164 [0.089, 0.199]`.
They are not interchangeable.

**Rule 88 — Before pricing any arm from a register census, state the base commit of both sides of
the census.** A census pair that spans a base change measures the base change.

### F117 — C-C IS DEAD, AND THE REASON IS A SECOND INSTANCE OF RULE 83

Three arithmetic-neutral restructures of the NA=5 body. `cc_scalarise` replaces `vec<float,NA>` with
`float[NA]` in the same elementwise order: g17s wide5 101 -> 100, wide3 89 -> 77, wide2 93 -> 74, but
**wide4 90 -> 101**, so the entry does not move. `cc_late_meta` moves the group scale and bias loads
after the inner `i` loop: wide5 101 -> 98, but wide3 89 -> 90 and wide4 90 -> 93. `cc_both` reaches
wide5 98 and drags wide4 to 98. Best C-C entry is 98 / 40 / `+2.56 %`, above the `<= 93` bar.

**The `applegpu_g17s` allocator prices the `vec<float,4>` and `vec<float,5>` forms in opposite
directions from the `applegpu_g16s` allocator, so every source transform that helps NA=5 hurts
NA=4.** C-C closed at its stated bar.

### F118 — C-B'S MECHANISM WAS WRONG

`case 2:` calls `qmv_fast_crossrow_affine4_g64<T, 2>`, the pair kernel at 89 registers, not a wide
body. Retiring it deletes something already below the maximum, so it changes nothing. The `wide<2>`
body enters through the `TAIL` branch of `<T,5,3,true>` because `5 % 3 == 2`. C-B's target number is
reachable; C-B's mechanism is not.

### RULE 89 — AN OCCUPANCY FIGURE DERIVED FROM A REGISTER COUNT IS A MODEL OUTPUT, NOT A MEASUREMENT

Alphonse's Correction 1, accepted in full. `sg == floor(BUDGET / regs)` is computed by
`e121_arms.simdgroups()` from the register count, so any census reporting it is restating its own
input. Askeladd's "three instruments, one answer" is three readings of the same register counts:
real agreement about registers, no evidence at all about resident simdgroups. The only other local
channel, `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup`, saturates at 1024 in every cell and cannot discriminate.

**Label every such figure `derived`. Only a timing response or a hardware occupancy counter can
promote it.** F100-F103's "confirmed by three independent instruments" is downgraded accordingly:
the register agreement stands, the simdgroup law is a model. Alphonse's rung 2 ladder is the only
design in the campaign that can put a timing response against it.

### RULE 90 — BEFORE PRICING ANY KERNEL-LEVEL ARM, PROVE WHICH ENTRY POINT THE SCORED PATH REACHES ON THE CURRENT BASE

A merged candidate-owned dispatch can retire an entry point without deleting a line of it. Name the
dispatching call sites and the guard that selects them, on the base the experiment will run on, and
state the measured or bounded cost share of that entry point. A cost share carried forward from
before a routing change is void.

Advisor source scout, zero GPU. F121 said `Qwen35MTP.swift` contains zero `qwen35Routed*` call

`Qwen35MTP.swift` owns only `fc` and the norms; the head's attention and MLP are the **same

`qwen35RoutedLinear`. Four head projections enter the wrapper and are rejected on **`m == 1`**,
because the draft chain is sequential — each draft's input is the previous draft's output
(`Qwen36MTPBlockSession.swift:1406-1412`) — so the head's decoder layer can never present more than
one activation row.

Claimed head dispatch set per draft step (to be verified by askeladd, E131 rung 1):

```

1   mtp.fc                    10240    5120  U32/4/64 affine  none         --        affine_qmv_fast ntg.x=S
2   layers.0.self_attn.q_proj  5120   12288  U32/4/64 affine  yes    reject m==1     affine_qmv_fast ntg.x=1
3   layers.0.self_attn.k_proj  5120    1024  BF16 DENSE       n/a          --        plain matmul
4   layers.0.self_attn.v_proj  5120    1024  BF16 DENSE       n/a          --        plain matmul
5   layers.0.self_attn.o_proj  6144    5120  U32/4/64 affine  yes    reject m==1     affine_qmv_fast ntg.x=1
6   layers.0.mlp gate+up       5120   34816  U32/4/64 affine  yes    reject m==1     affine_qmv_fast ntg.x=1
7   layers.0.mlp.down_proj    17408    5120  U32/4/64 affine  yes    reject m==1     affine_qmv_fast ntg.x=1
8   draft readout centroid     5120   12292  U32/2/64 affine  no     bits != 4       qmv_fast_singlerow_affine2_g64
9   draft readout leaf rows    5120   24584  U32/2/64 affine  no     gather prim     gather path
10  draft rerank 32 rows       5120      32  custom           n/a          --        qwen35DraftSelectedAffine4RerankKernel
```

Three sub-claims, in order of surprise:

- **K and V are BF16 dense at runtime.** The declared head ships `precision_islands.k/v.{weight,
  indices}` at `[1024,5120]` BF16 with I32 index sets of length 1024. Both index sets are therefore
  **complete permutations**, `isCompletePermutation` (`Qwen35.swift:3008-3021`) accepts them,
  `installExactQKVRows` takes the `_exactKVDenseW` branch (`:3054-3071`), and the affine-4 K/V pack
  is never built. If true, K/V is permanently outside every quantised-kernel lever we own, and 21 MB
  of BF16 streams per draft step where 5 MB of affine-4 would do. Do **not** act on it — E82 and
  E124 measured island removal as slower (`noislands` +0.366 %, `qonly` +1.801 %) and it is on the
  stop list — but it explains *why* those arms lost.
- **`mtp.fc` is the only unrouted quantised head projection and it is fully routable.** 10240 -> 5120,
  affine-4 g64, `bias: false`; `k % 512 == 0` (20 x 512), `n >= 4096`, `n % 8 == 0`,
  `w.dim(1) == 1280 == k/8`. `m = S = 1 + accepted_count(previous round)`, so on beagle it sits near
  4.8 and clears the `3...9` guard most rounds. Two call sites: `Qwen35MTP.swift:195` and `:229`,
  substituting `qwen35RoutedLinear(fc, ...)`. Semantically a no-op fallback because `fc.bias == nil`.
  **Value: +5 to +15 us per round interpolated from the E120 net table, about +0.01 to +0.05 % — one
  to two orders below Route B and probably below local noise.** It is two lines and free, so compose
  it onto a candidate that is already being measured; never schedule it standalone. Edge cases: the
  first drafting round of a leg flushes `seedTokenCount - 1` priming rows so `S ~ 512`, out of range,
  once per leg; on a mostly-serial prompt `S` accumulates across non-drafting rounds and can exceed
  9, above `get_qmv_batch_limit = 10`.
- **Rows 2, 5, 6, 7 all enter `affine_qmv_fast<bf16,64,4,false>` at `ntg.x == 1`**, hit
  `default: break` in the wide switch, and fall through to `qmv_fast_impl<T,64,4>`

body in that function, not the body that executes. Set every width to one pass and the widest

E63 (PR #66, ledger 15875-15950) fitted the old kernel as `t ~ a + b*NA + s*1[peak live > 128]`

-16.5 / -31.2 / -50.9 % grows monotonically with distance over the 128-register boundary. That is
the signature of `s`, not of the pass count.

E104 therefore did not measure the price of one pass. E104 measured the price of spilling a
shared switch.

### FINDING 134 — THE 542.8 GB/s M5 CEILING IS A PRE-E100 ARTEFACT, AND THE 2.8x ROOFLINE
### HEADROOM IS REFUTED

`research/finding22_reprice.py:21` states it verbatim: `RANKED_STREAM_RATE = 542.8  # GB/s,
28.8247 GB / 53108 us`. That is `2 * 14.4123 GB` over a ranked M=5 round time, computed when M=5
still dispatched `<T,5,3>` and therefore read the weights TWICE. Post-E100 the ranked M=5 round
is `G=1` and achieves 273.0 GB/s. Finding 31 lists 542.8 in a column labelled "ranked GB/s",
which is an ACHIEVED rate. Using the machine's own best observed cell as its ceiling forces that
cell to 100 % saturation by construction.

No STREAM figure for the ranked host exists or can exist in this repository: every g17s number
the campaign owns is offline compilation through `xcrun metal-tt`. Treat 546 GB/s as the highest
rate ever observed on any Apple part in scope, never as an M5 ceiling.

The "2.8x headroom to the memory roofline" I had been carrying is not a roofline measurement at
all. It is algebraically `2 * (M=8 round / M=5 round) = 2 * 74254.6 / 52791.9 = 2.8131`, with the
weight bytes and the machine bandwidth cancelling out. It contains no bandwidth information. That
is ADVISOR ERROR 107.

Corrected ranked achieved rates, round frame, under the current G table:

```
M   G   bytes GB   ranked us   ranked GB/s
1   1     14.41      31,182       462.2
5   1     14.41      52,792       273.0
8   2     28.82      74,255       388.2
```

M=1 is the fastest bytes-per-second cell on the ranked machine and M=8 is faster than M=5. There
is no 2.8x headroom at M=8 relative to M=5; the sign is the other way.

THE CORRECT INSTRUMENT IS WITHIN-SEGMENT INFLATION. Inside a fixed-G segment the bytes are
constant, so every extra microsecond is non-byte work:

```
ranked G=1, M=1 -> M=4 : 31,182 -> 43,081 us  = +38.2 %  for zero extra bytes
ranked G=2, M=6 -> M=8 : 59,946 -> 74,255 us  = +23.9 %  for zero extra bytes
```

If arithmetic were free, M=8 at the M=6 byte rate saves 19.3 % of the M=8 round and M=4 at the
M=1 rate saves 27.6 % of the M=4 round. These are upper bounds that also contain occupancy and
issue rate. Build on 19 to 28 % within-segment envelopes, never on 2.8x.

This is consistent with Finding 31's own conclusion: at NA=5 the kernel reads at roughly 55 % of
DRAM peak and computes at roughly 47 % of the FMA ceiling AT THE SAME TIME. Neither resource is
exhausted. It is a latency or issue-rate problem.

#### FINDING 134.2 — THE ACCUMULATION-ORDER WALL, RESTATED WITH ITS RECEIPT

No change to floating-point accumulation order in the target verify path is safe, and the
campaign has already measured why. Ledger 8794-8801: ONE CHARACTER OF REASSOCIATION MOVED
DECLARED TOP-TWO ROW EVIDENCE AT 52 OF 64 POSITIONS, with top-1 flips zero, while the local run
reported `all_tokens_matched=true`, `residual_divergence_count=0` and
`public_drift_tripwire_passed=true`. The local legs generate their own reference rows from the
candidate binary, so the parity line cannot see a row-evidence move.

The only admissible evidence for an order change is a per-position row-evidence digest showing
ZERO moved rows over the full 512-token window, which is the definition of bit-exact. The only
safe accumulation-order change is no change. Route B is built that way for exactly this reason,
and `quantized.h:820-822`, `quantized.h:965-967` and `Qwen35.swift:1406-1408` all state it as the
design contract. Promote this to RULE 92.
